a15.speaker: Amos Anias, Congolese refugee
a15.name: Amos Anias
a15.title: Congolese refugee
a15.speech: "I know the World Refugee Day; it's our day to celebrate and get more recognition," ; "However, it is also a day for the entire international community to recognize the value of peace, join hands for peace, and support efforts to bring peace to my country, the DR Congo, so that my fellow refugees and I can go back home soon,"

a15.speaker: Amos Anias, Congolese refugee
a15.name: Amos Anias
a15.title: Congolese refugee
a15.speech: "I'm happy I received food assistance since 2012 when I was relocated from Nkamira transit centre to this Kigeme camp. I receive in-kind food assistance and switched to new modality of receiving food assistance in form of cash-based transfers in 2014 to buy food of my choice," ; "It was during this time that I joined a refugee savings scheme, saving RWF 1,000 per month for a year. After one year, our savings group had accumulated nearly RWF 200,000, and I applied for a short loan of RWF 50,000 to start small-scale mushroom farming inside Kigeme camp."

a15.speaker: Dr Mutinta Hambayi, WFP's acting Country Director
a15.name: Dr Mutinta Hambayi
a15.title: WFP's acting Country Director
a15.speech: "Increasing the household income contributes to improved dietary diversity and nutrition for the families in the refugee camps,"

a16.speaker: Aurélie Adam Soulé, Minister of Digital Affairs and Digitalization
a16.name: Aurélie Adam Soulé
a16.title: Minister of Digital Affairs and Digitalization
a16.speech: Specified that after the various visits over the past year, she wants to ensure that "the desired transformations to offer a work environment meeting international standards are taken into account and that deadlines will be respected by the contractor."

a16.speaker: Janvier Yahouédéou, deputy minister for economic affairs and digital affairs
a16.name: Janvier Yahouédéou
a16.title: deputy minister for economic affairs and digital affairs
a16.speech: "These works, from a broader point of view, are part of the dynamic of a Benin that is reinventing itself. A dynamic in which every idea, every project places a point of honor on quality so that our television meets international standards,"

a447.speaker: Elon Musk, close advisor to Trump and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a447.name: Elon Musk
a447.title: close advisor to Trump and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a447.speech: Declared that USAID will be “shutting down” as part of a broader initiative to reduce the size of the federal government ; described USAID as “a criminal organisation” and asserted, “you’ve got to basically get rid of the whole thing” ; described USAID as “a viper’s nest of radical-left Marxists who hate America” ; claimed to have received full agreement from Trump on the need to dismantle USAID, stating, “I went over with him in detail, and he agreed that we should shut it down”.

a447.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a447.name: Donald Trump
a447.title: US President
a447.speech: Criticised USAID’s management and suggested that it has been “run by a bunch of radical lunatics.”

a447.speaker: Elizabeth Warren, US Senator
a447.name: Elizabeth Warren
a447.title: US Senator
a447.speech: Condemned the actions taken by Musk and Trump, warning that they risk compromising essential government functions and access to sensitive information, and stated, “We must do everything in our power to push back and protect people from harm.”

a555.speaker: Justin Dovoédo, communication director of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Benin)
a555.name: Justin Dovoédo
a555.title: communication director of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Benin)
a555.speech: Made a plea for a new form of collaboration; invited the director general and her staff to reflect on a new form of partnership that would not necessarily oblige the MCA to put up money.

a555.speaker: Mélanie Roe, director of communication operations for the Millennium Challenge Corporation (Washington)
a555.name: Mélanie Roe
a555.title: director of communication operations for the Millennium Challenge Corporation (Washington)
a555.speech: Said she wanted to see how ONIP works, particularly the newspaper "La Nation," and in what framework to continue the communication collaboration in support of the second MCA-Benin compact; wanted to know whether the energy component is essential enough to merit the support of the newspaper "La Nation."

a555.speaker: Reine Azifan, acting director general of the National Printing and Press Office (ONIP)
a555.name: Reine Azifan
a555.title: acting director general of the National Printing and Press Office (ONIP)
a555.speech: Thanked her guests for the honour paid to her institution; explained the functioning of the newspaper "La Nation," which, although a public service body, has financial autonomy, meaning salary and operating costs are the responsibility of the office, so there is always a counterpart, a kind of win-win partnership between ONIP and the institutions that request its support; however, organisations such as the MCA which invest in development are not treated on the same footing as commercial enterprises. She gave the example of UNICEF, which partnered with "La Nation" for media coverage of its activities and in return supports ONIP with computer equipment, cameras and recorders.

a555.speaker: Bruno Sèwadé, editor-in-chief of "La Nation", and Marie-Madeleine Akoffodji, head of ONIP's commercial department
a555.name: Bruno Sèwadé
a555.title: editor-in-chief of "La Nation", and Marie-Madeleine Akoffodji, head of ONIP's commercial department
a555.speech: Gave assurances that the energy problem is crucial given the power cuts Benin has been going through for years; pleaded for access to energy for all, but at an acceptable cost.

a582.speaker: Shaun van Rooi, Medical Rescue 911 (press statement)
a582.name: Shaun van Rooi
a582.title: Medical Rescue 911 (press statement)
a582.speech: Explains that the initiative sprung from the fact that the pandemic is crippling the nation ; "Medical Rescue 911 is thus calling on all communities to be part of this drive to help our fellow Namibians fight this dread virus" ; further explained that there is a lot that goes into setting up a medical centre of that magnitude and will rely on the generous donations to renovate building, donation of medical beds and medical equipment ; "The Khomasdal medical centre for Covid-19 will be able to accommodate 10 severe patients on a four hourly basis" ; further said the initiative is a voluntary project and the assistance of the community in that regard will be crucial to help make it a success.

a681.speaker: Barclays (new report by the British bank)
a681.name: Barclays (new report by the British bank)
a681.speech: According to a new report by Barclays, Senegal's public debt now reaches 119% of its GDP, nearly double the regional average in sub-Saharan Africa, significantly higher than the 99.7% cited in a recent national audit.

a681.speaker: Recent Senegalese national audit (report)
a681.name: Recent Senegalese national audit (report)
a681.speech: Cited a public debt figure of 99.7% of GDP.

a681.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a681.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a681.title: President of Senegal
a681.speech: Ordered a general audit of the hidden debts of the previous administration.

a785.speaker: Communities in Traditional Authorities Chamba and Ntonda, Mangochi district
a785.name: Communities in Traditional Authorities Chamba and Ntonda
a785.title: Mangochi district
a785.speech: Have commended the Titukulane Resilience Food Security Activity for constructing new and rehabilitating existing, but dysfunctional, boreholes in the two areas.

a785.speaker: Village Head Chiyambeni, under T/A Ntonda
a785.name: Village Head Chiyambeni
a785.title: under T/A Ntonda
a785.speech: Said the problem of lack of safe and clean drinking water negatively affected the social and economic development of his area, and stated that the high levels of destitution and poverty in the area are a result of lack of water, observing that without safe and clean drinking water the possibility of breaking out of the cycle of poverty is incredibly slim: "Lack of water and poverty are inseparably linked because where there is no water, able-bodied members of a community are forced to spend hours searching and transporting water instead of working on their farms. Additionally, poor access to water and insufficient sanitation affect the health of the poor, their food security, and their prospects for making a living."

a785.speaker: Village Head Chiyambeni, under T/A Ntonda
a785.name: Village Head Chiyambeni
a785.title: under T/A Ntonda
a785.speech: Emphasized that the construction and rehabilitation of the boreholes have reduced cases of waterborne diseases in the targeted areas: "We will now actively participate in the social and economic activities taking place in our communities."

a785.speaker: Theresa Kananji, 50, a widow from Chiyambeni Village who lost her husband to cholera
a785.name: Theresa Kananji
a785.title: 50, a widow from Chiyambeni Village who lost her husband to cholera
a785.speech: Said her spouse would not have died if the village had access to safe and clean drinking water, and described the construction of the borehole as a great relief and salvation not only to her family but also to the entire village: "I am very excited with the coming in of a borehole in our village. We used to walk long distances to fetch water from unsafe sources. It would take three hours for someone to walk to and from the water source." ; "This borehole will significantly reduce cases of cases of cholera and other waterborne diseases thereby saving lives. We're very grateful to Care International in Malawi and its partners for giving us this precious gift."

a785.speaker: Solomon Chirwa, WaterAid Malawi Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) specialist
a785.name: Solomon Chirwa
a785.title: WaterAid Malawi Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) specialist
a785.speech: Said the project has helped significantly in improving knowledge, attitudes, skills and norms related to essential sanitation and hygiene behaviors, and stated that there is now increased availability of basic safely managed facilities and consumables necessary for essential sanitation and hygiene practices: "Through the same project, we also provided technical assistance in WASH policy review, WASH planning including integrated planning and performance review with other sectors especially at policy and district levels. We also advocated for increased funding for the WASH sector that recognizes and promotes complementarity with other sectors such as health, education and gender."

a819.speaker: Sammy Gyamfi, Acting CEO of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod)
a819.name: Sammy Gyamfi
a819.title: Acting CEO of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod)
a819.speech: Thanked the companies and the Chamber of Mines for their cooperation, stating that the agreement aligns with President John Mahama’s vision to optimize national benefits from gold resources; indicated that this agreement is part of the GoldBod’s bid to boost gold and foreign reserve accumulation by the Bank of Ghana in line with the vision of the President.

a885.speaker: Namibian Police
a885.name: Namibian Police
a885.speech: Have asked young people to stop smoking the pipe known as “Hubbly Bubbly”, which is used mostly by young people, saying it is regarded as dangerous.

a885.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Namibian Minister of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
a885.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a885.title: Namibian Minister of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
a885.speech: Warned young people at drinking spots: “Do you know that what you are smoking is dangerous? It destroys your health, and you are still young children” ; said it would be good if they stopped smoking hubbly because it is dangerous.

a885.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Namibian Minister of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
a885.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a885.title: Namibian Minister of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
a885.speech: Explained that the purpose of visiting the young people that day was to get close to them and teach them what is right: “It works better when people are advised while they are still in good spirits, so that they are able to distinguish what is right from what is wrong.”

a885.speaker: Elias Mutota, Deputy Inspector General of the Namibian Police
a885.name: Elias Mutota
a885.title: Deputy Inspector General of the Namibian Police
a885.speech: Said he had noticed that at many of the drinking places he visited that day there were young people smoking hubbly, but that it is often mixed with drugs ; “Young people are using their time badly, so we are asking them to stop smoking it because it is dangerous. Those who manufacture that thing do not use it themselves, yet Namibians embrace it.”

a885.speaker: Elias Mutota, Deputy Inspector General of the Namibian Police
a885.name: Elias Mutota
a885.title: Deputy Inspector General of the Namibian Police
a885.speech: Added that the government is in the process of making a law to ban hubbly from being used in this country, and said they want hubbly to end so that they can have young people who are on the right path in the future, because hubbly destroys them.

a904.speaker: Group Village Head (GVH) Kalonga, Milton Village, TA Mbenje, Nsanje District
a904.name: Group Village Head (GVH) Kalonga
a904.title: Milton Village, TA Mbenje, Nsanje District
a904.speech: Appealed to government to construct an irrigation scheme so that the relocated people can be food secure, asking for this life-changing facility on behalf of her subjects ; said despite their settling at the upper land, her subjects have been hit hard by hunger following last year’s dry spell: “We have farmland at Makhanga but it is in water due to rising levels of water in Shire River.” ; added that once the scheme is constructed, families will be able to grow crops more than once a year, contributing to food security at household level.

a904.speaker: Group Village Head (GVH) Kalonga
a904.name: Group Village Head (GVH) Kalonga
a904.speech: Assured the delegation that the community will never go back to Makhanga after going through devastating floods every year, and praised a non-governmental organisation called Give Direct for supporting the community with startup cash which the community used to build houses at the new settlement area.

a904.speaker: Olympia Wereko-Brobby, British Deputy High Commissioner in Malawi
a904.name: Olympia Wereko-Brobby
a904.title: British Deputy High Commissioner in Malawi
a904.speech: Commended the community for using the donation wisely: “I am impressed the way the community build its resilient following the effects of Cyclone Freddy.”

a904.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Commissioner for Disaster (DoDMA)
a904.name: Charles Kalemba
a904.title: Commissioner for Disaster (DoDMA)
a904.speech: Said the government was putting in place sustainable systems to ensure food security in the country: “Such systems include irrigation schemes just like what we have seen at Chimwala mbango scheme which is gravity fed”, while assuring the community that the government will continue supporting them with systems that will enhance food security in Nsanje.

a915.speaker: Nancy Tembo, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malawi
a915.name: Nancy Tembo
a915.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malawi
a915.speech: Has expressed gratitude to the United States government for its ongoing support in Malawi’s social and economic development, and highlighted the significant contributions made by the US since Malawi’s independence in 1964 ; noted that the US has been the largest bilateral donor to Malawi, providing assistance in key sectors such as education, health, agriculture, and research through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

a915.speaker: Amy Diaz, US Chief of Mission in Malawi
a915.name: Amy Diaz
a915.title: US Chief of Mission in Malawi
a915.speech: Emphasized the vital role the US has played in shaping Malawi’s development journey, including supporting smallholder farmers, strengthening health systems, and promoting democracy ; reaffirmed the US’s commitment to continued partnership and development in Malawi, stating that the US stands with the Malawian people in addressing systemic challenges.

a963.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a963.name: Donald Trump
a963.title: US President
a963.speech: showered Musk with praise for his work as the head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE); he credited Musk with delivering “a colossal change in the old ways of doing business in Washington” and called Musk’s service “without comparison in modern history” ; assured reporters that DOGE would continue its work even after Musk is gone: “With Elon’s guidance, [DOGE is] helping to detect fraud, slash waste and modernise broken and outdated systems” ; “Elon’s really not leaving. He’s going to be back and forth, I think.”

a963.speaker: Elon Musk, outgoing head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a963.name: Elon Musk
a963.title: outgoing head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a963.speech: declined to comment on the New York Times report during his Oval Office appearance and avoided remarking on speculation that his departure was connected to tumbling sales at Tesla; instead he pointed out that, as a special government employee, he cannot work in the Trump administration for a period exceeding 130 days without facing stricter disclosure and ethics requirements ; “This is not the end of DOGE, but really at the beginning. The DOGE team will only grow stronger over time.” ; maintained that $1 trillion in savings remained a long-term goal: “I’m confident that over time, we’ll see a trillion dollars of savings, a reduction – a trillion dollars of waste and fraud reduction.” ; explained that he felt DOGE had become seen as a “boogeyman”, blamed for any effort to overhaul the federal government, but reaffirmed his commitment to being a “friend and adviser to the president” and said the experience was worthwhile: “I think it was. I think [it] was an important thing. I think it was a necessary thing, and I think it will have a good effect in the future.”

a963.speaker: Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a963.name: Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a963.speech: As of Friday, the panel claimed it had achieved an estimated $175bn in savings, made up of “asset sales, contract/lease cancellations and renegotiations, fraud and improper payment deletion, grant cancellations, interest savings, programmatic changes, regulatory savings, and workforce reductions”.

a963.speaker: Reuters analysis (news agency)
a963.name: Reuters analysis (news agency)
a963.speech: An analysis published on Friday by the news agency Reuters suggests the actual sum is much lower; using US Treasury summaries, Reuters found that only $19bn in federal spending had been cut, though it noted that some savings may require more time to be reflected in the Treasury Department’s data.

a963.speaker: The New York Times (report)
a963.name: The New York Times (report)
a963.speech: published a report alleging that Musk has struggled with increasing drug use and personal turmoil behind the scenes.

a1150.speaker: Bogolo Kenewendo, Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.name: Bogolo Kenewendo
a1150.title: Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.speech: Said Botswana currently generates about 65 percent of its electricity needs while the remaining supply is imported from neighbouring countries, including South Africa ; "The availability and reliability of our existing power plants, Morupule A and Morupule B, are key to the security of supply in the short to medium-term."

a1150.speaker: Bogolo Kenewendo, Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.name: Bogolo Kenewendo
a1150.title: Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.speech: Said part of the government's strategy involves major coal-fired power projects to meet the country's energy needs. She noted that the 600-megawatt coal-fired power plant at Mmamabule is now under development and is expected to be operational by 2027 ; Said Morupule A, which was refurbished in 2016, will be decommissioned in 2028 once sufficient base load is secured, and the site may be repurposed for clean energy generation.

a1150.speaker: Bogolo Kenewendo, Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.name: Bogolo Kenewendo
a1150.title: Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.speech: "The ministry is making notable progress, albeit rather slowly, in transforming our power generation sources from predominantly coal to solar primary energy resources." ; Disclosed that the first large scale solar project, Phase 1 of the 50-megawatt Mmadinare Solar Cluster, began commercial operation on 12 March 2025.

a1150.speaker: Bogolo Kenewendo, Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.name: Bogolo Kenewendo
a1150.title: Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.speech: Said the private sector is leading the development of the renewable energy projects, with Botswana Power Corporation (BPC) serving as the offtaker under long-term power purchase agreements of up to 25 years. She said foreign investors are required to partner with Botswana-owned companies, holding at least 40 percent of project shares, and that small-scale solar PV projects remain exclusively reserved for 100 percent citizen-owned businesses.

a1150.speaker: Bogolo Kenewendo, Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.name: Bogolo Kenewendo
a1150.title: Minister of Minerals and Energy of Botswana
a1150.speech: "To improve the performance of the electricity supply industry and ensure its sustainability, the ministry is reviewing the electricity supply industry structure."

a1186.speaker: Official announcement (unattributed)
a1186.name: Official announcement (unattributed)
a1186.speech: It was officially announced that a ceasefire agreement between Hamas and Israel would take effect next Sunday at 12:15, following intense regional and international mediation aimed at containing the escalation and ending the growing cycle of violence in the territory.

a1186.speaker: Israeli media
a1186.name: Israeli media
a1186.speech: Information relayed by the Israeli media indicates that Hamas will resume control of the Gaza Strip during the implementation of the planned exchange agreement, until another arrangement takes over.

a1186.speaker: Certain sources (anonymous)
a1186.name: Certain sources (anonymous)
a1186.speech: Report that Gulf countries, foremost among them Kuwait, had already expressed their willingness to take part in the reconstruction of the Gaza Strip from the beginning of the war, which was fairly well received in local circles.

a1186.speaker: Egypt
a1186.name: Egypt
a1186.speech: Proposed the creation of a support committee composed of independent figures to administer Gaza.

a1186.speaker: Palestinian National Authority
a1186.name: Palestinian National Authority
a1186.speech: Firmly rejected Egypt's proposal and insists on resuming the management of the territory without sharing it or using any intermediary body.

a1186.speaker: Unnamed official
a1186.name: Unnamed official
a1186.speech: Confirmed that the Rafah commercial crossing will resume operations from next Sunday, to receive trucks loaded with humanitarian aid and various goods.

a1186.speaker: Reliable sources (anonymous)
a1186.name: Reliable sources (anonymous)
a1186.speech: Indicate that the 2005 agreement will be restored, which stipulates that the management of the Rafah crossing will be entrusted to Israel and the Palestinian National Authority, with the presence of international observers.

a1186.speaker: Donald Trump, former US President
a1186.name: Donald Trump
a1186.title: former US President
a1186.speech: Statements on "achieving peace through force in the Middle East."

a1303.speaker: Elected deputy national officials of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)
a1303.name: Elected deputy national officials of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)
a1303.speech: Declared their support for the Acting National Chairman, Ambassador Umar Damagum-led camp within the NWC, and asked the other members of the NWC who are against Damagum to stop spoiling the name of the party through their criticism of the acting Chairman, saying that he cannot be removed until his tenure of the NWC ends in December.

a1303.speaker: Timothy Osadolor, PDP deputy national youth leader
a1303.name: Timothy Osadolor
a1303.title: PDP deputy national youth leader
a1303.speech: Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters in Abuja on Wednesday, speaking on behalf of other deputies, said the tenure of the chairman has been settled till December 2025, while calling on members demarketing the party to stop and give Damagum the chance to reposition the PDP.

a1303.speaker: Timothy Osadolor, PDP deputy national youth leader
a1303.name: Timothy Osadolor
a1303.title: PDP deputy national youth leader
a1303.speech: On the battle for the National Secretary, between Samuel Anyanwu and Sunday Ude-Okoye, said the case is still in the court, adding that Senator Samuel Anyanwu remains the national secretary until the court decides otherwise.

a1303.speaker: Timothy Osadolor, PDP deputy national youth leader
a1303.name: Timothy Osadolor
a1303.title: PDP deputy national youth leader
a1303.speech: Called on the party members to come together and return the PDP to power in 2027, saying the National Working Committee remains intact and willing to work and to put PDP in good stead for future elections.

a1321.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1321.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1321.speech: According to the WHO, malaria is a life-threatening disease caused by parasites that are transmitted to people through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

a1321.speaker: National Malaria Elimination Centre (NMEC), Zambia
a1321.name: National Malaria Elimination Centre (NMEC)
a1321.title: Zambia
a1321.speech: Said that on average there are an estimated 20,000 cases of malaria per day in Zambia, and each day an average of four Zambians die from the killer disease.

a1321.speaker: Elijah Muchima, Zambian Minister of Health
a1321.name: Elijah Muchima
a1321.title: Zambian Minister of Health
a1321.speech: Says Government is working with other cooperating partners and neighbouring countries to end malaria by 2030. "It is the desire of this Government that by 2030 we end malaria. It is our number one agenda in the ministry, working together with other countries because we cannot just deal with it in Zambia. You have also to go to the neighbours collectively."

a1321.speaker: Idah Mumba, community health worker from Mansa district, Luapula Province
a1321.name: Idah Mumba
a1321.title: community health worker from Mansa district, Luapula Province
a1321.speech: Disclosed that she serves 224 households in her community in providing malaria tests, family planning, and maternal health support. "My coverage community has 987 people. The long distances were my biggest challenge. However, with a bicycle, I can now reach more families and deliver care on time." ; Stressed that early diagnosis and treatment of malaria helps prevent local transmission of the disease and stop the progression of malaria cases from uncomplicated to complicated forms that can be fatal ; Thanked Amref for its support in providing a bicycle which has enhanced her service delivery, visiting more households and improving community health.

a1321.speaker: Anthony Gitau, Johnson and Johnson's director of programme delivery and impact for Africa and the Middle East
a1321.name: Anthony Gitau
a1321.title: Johnson and Johnson's director of programme delivery and impact for Africa and the Middle East
a1321.speech: Stressed the importance of investing in community health to deliver universal health coverage (UHC) ; underscored the urgency of using limited resources efficiently, given the global shortage of six million health workers, two million of whom are community health workers.

a1321.speaker: Landry Dongmo Tsague, Centre for Diseases Control-Africa representative
a1321.name: Landry Dongmo Tsague
a1321.title: Centre for Diseases Control-Africa representative
a1321.speech: Commended community health workers' dedication and emphasised the importance of investing in resilient health systems, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic ; called for mobilisation of domestic resources to be used to train, equip, digitise, and remunerate CHWs in Africa ; "We must invest in community health workers as the primary health workforce. We should not consider the CH as a second-class workforce, but rather, as a front-line workforce."

a1321.speaker: World Bicycle Relief (organisation/data)
a1321.name: World Bicycle Relief (organisation/data)
a1321.speech: According to World Bicycle Relief, in Zambia, CHWs equipped with bicycles reported a 63 percent increase in productivity, enabling them to reach more patients and improve maternal and child health outcomes.

a1321.speaker: Maureen Kolenyo, World Bicycle Relief representative
a1321.name: Maureen Kolenyo
a1321.title: World Bicycle Relief representative
a1321.speech: Detailed the impact of bicycle solutions on CHW productivity, noting that her organisation has distributed over 868,000 bicycles. "Bicycles are affordable, efficient, have low impact on the environment and are easy to use. We have insurmountable evidence to show that they transform health care delivery. A study in Zambia showed a 63 percent increase in service delivery where CHWs had bicycles. That's the power of mobility."

a1321.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa group chief executive officer
a1321.name: Githinji Gitahi
a1321.title: Amref Health Africa group chief executive officer
a1321.speech: Urged African leaders and global stakeholders to rethink health investments to build resilient and sustainable health systems ; underlined that Africa's economic and population growth challenges are deeply linked to healthcare financing ; "Sub-Saharan Africa is facing an economic crisis, and the lack of fiscal space is a major issue. Investing in health must be tied to population development, ensuring that every girl and woman has the right to make informed reproductive health choices." ; called for investment shifts towards Primary Health Care (PHC), warning that disproportionate funding for tertiary care leaves millions without access to essential services.

a1321.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa group chief executive officer
a1321.name: Githinji Gitahi
a1321.title: Amref Health Africa group chief executive officer
a1321.speech: Noted that Amref had significant programmes worth about US$28 million in Kenya, Malawi, Zambia and Ethiopia that were being sponsored by USAID, and that the core of these programmes was around maternal and child health, preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission. "So, as we speak, we are working with the governments to ensure that no child is going to be exposed to HIV because they were not protected during the mother's pregnancy. That's a risk." ; "We had programmes on HIV prevention testing, for example, we had programmes on what you may call running care treatment centres for HIV, what we call the comprehensive care clinics that have stopped." ; Said Amref had health workers across Zambia, Malawi, Ethiopia and Kenya, among other countries, that were actively involved in care and treatment for prevention of mother-to-child HIV and tuberculosis transmission, care and prevention that are out of the health system, though they are still trained.

a1520.speaker: USAID Malawi
a1520.name: USAID Malawi
a1520.speech: Has ordered its implementing partners to immediately stop all work under the Malawi funding agreement, citing an Executive Order issued by US President Donald Trump.

a1520.speaker: Executive Order issued by US President Donald Trump
a1520.name: Executive Order issued by US President Donald Trump
a1520.speech: The order aimed to reevaluate and realign US foreign aid to ensure it aligns with American national interests.

a1520.speaker: Maziko Matemba, Executive Director for Health and Rights Education Program Malawi
a1520.name: Maziko Matemba
a1520.title: Executive Director for Health and Rights Education Program Malawi
a1520.speech: Warning of a "big blow" to the health sector; his organization is directly affected by the funding freeze, which will impact demand creation for HIV and health services, as well as recruitment and payment of civil servants in the health sector ; "This is a critical moment for Malawi's health sector" ; "We urge the government to provide a clear plan to fill the resulting gap, ensuring that girls and women continue to access Sexual Reproductive Health Rights Services and preventing new HIV infections." ; "We need to ensure that the health sector continues to receive the support it needs to deliver essential services to the people of Malawi."

a1520.speaker: US Government Accountability Office (report)
a1520.name: US Government Accountability Office (report)
a1520.speech: "Field operations will not return to previous implementation levels until at least fiscal year 2043" ; The report highlights the challenges faced by USAID and its partners in navigating the funding freeze.

a1537.speaker: Dr. Samukeliso Dube, Executive Director of FP2030
a1537.name: Dr. Samukeliso Dube
a1537.title: Executive Director of FP2030
a1537.speech: Emphasises that family planning is not merely a health service but a fundamental human right that must be prioritised, especially in light of recent global cuts in foreign aid.

a1537.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) research
a1537.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) research
a1537.speech: Indicates that for every dollar invested in family planning, there is an estimated return of $8.78 in benefits to families and society, translating into a potential economic benefit of approximately N1.06 trillion ($660 billion) by 2050.

a1537.speaker: FP2030 "Made Possible by Family Planning" campaign
a1537.name: FP2030 "Made Possible by Family Planning" campaign
a1537.speech: Calls for a unified effort from all sectors — government officials, community leaders, and citizens — and aims to raise $1 billion by 2025 to enhance access to rights-based family planning services, reinforcing the notion that family planning should be perceived as an investment rather than a cost; it seeks to galvanise new leadership and funding, and to shift the narrative surrounding family planning from a taboo subject to a celebrated aspect of modern life by engaging influencers from the arts, sports and fashion.

a1537.speaker: International Conference on Family Planning (ICFP) 2025 (organisers/theme)
a1537.name: International Conference on Family Planning (ICFP) 2025 (organisers/theme)
a1537.speech: Set the theme "Equity Through Action: Advancing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights for All" for the conference taking place in Bogotá, Colombia, from November 3–6, 2025.

a1657.speaker: 2025 Chandler Good Government Index (CGGI) report
a1657.name: 2025 Chandler Good Government Index (CGGI) report
a1657.speech: notes that Tanzania's improved ranking is largely due to the government's increasing adoption of new policy solutions and reform strategies, particularly in the Leadership and Foresight pillar: "The Tanzanian government's increasing adoption of new policy solutions and reform strategies corresponds with notable rank gains in the Leadership and Foresight pillar" ; also highlights Tanzania's commitment to more reliable and predictable government policies, alongside strengthened diplomatic ties with countries such as Egypt, France and Türkiye ; "Tanzania's foreign and domestic investment surged 21.6 per cent, reaching 6.56 billion US dollars (about 16tri/-) in the fiscal year ending June 2024."

a1657.speaker: CGGI report (statement)
a1657.name: CGGI report (statement)
a1657.speech: noted that Financial Stewardship has seen the most sustained decline due to tightening fiscal conditions and rising government debt burdens in many countries.

a1657.speaker: Sakina Mwinyimkuu, Director of the Division of Performance Monitoring and Evaluation in the Prime Minister's Office (Policy, Parliament and Coordination)
a1657.name: Sakina Mwinyimkuu
a1657.title: Director of the Division of Performance Monitoring and Evaluation in the Prime Minister's Office (Policy, Parliament and Coordination)
a1657.speech: attributed the country's success to stable and effective leadership under President Samia Suluhu Hassan, especially through her 4Rs philosophy (Reconciliation, Resilience, Reforms and Rebuilding): "These four principles frame, guide and focus everything we do in government" ; noted that the government has established key institutions to guide Tanzania's economic transformation, including the Planning Commission, created under the Planning Commission Act of 2023.

a1657.speaker: Dr Isaac Safari, economist and political analyst at Saint Augustine University of Tanzania (SAUT)
a1657.name: Dr Isaac Safari
a1657.title: economist and political analyst at Saint Augustine University of Tanzania (SAUT)
a1657.speech: praised President Samia for embracing participatory governance, noting that this approach has strengthened the Leadership and Foresight pillar ; commended the sixth-phase government for its commitment to transparency, the rule of law and the separation of powers, which have been essential in promoting justice and accountability ; regarding the improvement in the Attractive Marketplace pillar, noted the government's prioritisation of economic diplomacy as a driving force for attracting investment and fostering business growth.

a1657.speaker: Hamiduni Maliseli, political analyst
a1657.name: Hamiduni Maliseli
a1657.title: political analyst
a1657.speech: said the report underscores the government's ongoing efforts to advance democratic governance and improve people's welfare: "This globally recognised report serves as a reminder of Tanzania's leadership strides, for those who may have doubted the country's progress" ; urged other countries in the region to adopt Tanzania's methods, particularly the 4Rs philosophy, as a model for improving leadership and governance.

a1798.speaker: Getnet Worku, expert at the National Biosafety Advisory Committee (Ethiopia)
a1798.name: Getnet Worku
a1798.title: expert at the National Biosafety Advisory Committee (Ethiopia)
a1798.speech: Told Capital that the main aim of the trial is to see how well the GMO maize resists drought and insects. "We need to upscale our maize production and the best way is to use a better seed which both resists water shortages and insects. If we get positive results on the trail we will carry out more over the next five years. If the seeds don't have a problem with the environment and soil we will used them commercially."

a1843.speaker: Teyba Jemal, 36-year-old maid queuing for bread in the Lafto neighbourhood
a1843.name: Teyba Jemal
a1843.title: 36-year-old maid queuing for bread in the Lafto neighbourhood
a1843.speech: "Either I buy this or not eat," Teyba told Fortune.

a1843.speaker: Adamu Mulat, Sheger Bread distributor
a1843.name: Adamu Mulat
a1843.title: Sheger Bread distributor
a1843.speech: "I don't blame them. The bread is not enough for all." ; On the volume of bread received at his outlet: "It all depends on the supply."

a1843.speaker: Hussien Ahmed, significant shareholder of Mizan Flour & Biscuit Factory
a1843.name: Hussien Ahmed
a1843.title: significant shareholder of Mizan Flour & Biscuit Factory
a1843.speech: Was in despair about the meagre wheat supply that has led the factory to operate at 20pc of capacity, saying he had to let go of seven of his 47 employees and had to source wheat with the help of intermediaries, paying an additional price of up to 5,000 Br: "Consumers shoulder the burden."

a1843.speaker: Muluneh Lema, head of the Ethiopian Millers' Association
a1843.name: Muluneh Lema
a1843.title: head of the Ethiopian Millers' Association
a1843.speech: Said the Association's leaders tried to commission a survey of the millers but many declined to participate for fear of consequences: "The scarcity is not recent."

a1843.speaker: Endeshaw Legesse, director of procurement, Ethiopian Industrial Inputs Development Enterprise (EIIDE)
a1843.name: Endeshaw Legesse
a1843.title: director of procurement, Ethiopian Industrial Inputs Development Enterprise (EIIDE)
a1843.speech: Attributed the challenges to farmers' unions directly supplying the government and cutting the cord of the distribution chain.

a1843.speaker: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD) and Shimelis Abdisa, head of the Oromia Regional State
a1843.name: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD) and Shimelis Abdisa
a1843.title: head of the Oromia Regional State
a1843.speech: Announced two weeks ago the first batch of 1.2 million quintals harvested in the Bale Zone.

a1843.speaker: Oromia Regional State officials
a1843.name: Oromia Regional State officials
a1843.speech: Claim to have 2.8 million hectares of land cultivated in the region, and continue to aspire to ensure 15 million quintals of wheat are shipped to East African markets such as Kenya, Djibouti, and Somalia.

a1843.speaker: Study commissioned by the USAID Ethiopia office on the wheat market
a1843.name: Study commissioned by the USAID Ethiopia office on the wheat market
a1843.speech: Concluded that Ethiopia would be unlikely to achieve a seven million tonnes harvest in five years; the study says Ethiopian farmers will find it difficult to plough over 2.1 million hectares of land.

a1843.speaker: Report by the Foreign Agricultural Services Bureau of the US Department of Agriculture
a1843.name: Report by the Foreign Agricultural Services Bureau of the US Department of Agriculture
a1843.speech: Has projected Ethiopia's wheat production for the current year at 5.5 million tonnes, a volume three times lower than what Ethiopian agriculture authorities wanted to see.

a1843.speaker: Mohammed Amanalo, 37, farmer in the Bale zone
a1843.name: Mohammed Amanalo
a1843.title: 37, farmer in the Bale zone
a1843.speech: Said he sold 420Qtl of wheat for 3,200 Br a quintal under the pressure of the local authorities: "We can't say no to the government."

a1843.speaker: Alemu Tesema, 50, farmer near Bishoftu (DebreZeit) town, Oromia Regional State
a1843.name: Alemu Tesema
a1843.title: 50, farmer near Bishoftu (DebreZeit) town, Oromia Regional State
a1843.speech: Was discontented with the regional bureau selling price officials set at 3,200 Br for a quintal, saying the price fails to consider the production costs, such as pesticides and labour put in during harvest, and that during several meetings with local authorities farmers' complaints have fallen on deaf ears: "No one wants to get less than what they spent."

a1843.speaker: Beriso Feyisa, deputy head of the Oromia Agriculture Bureau
a1843.name: Beriso Feyisa
a1843.title: deputy head of the Oromia Agriculture Bureau
a1843.speech: Claims the farmgate price exceeds production costs, describing the margin for farmers as "reasonable", crediting the Bureau for supplying agricultural inputs with loans, and disclosed the current export generating 50 dollars from a quintal, revealing a 700 Br loss from the farmgate price: "The forex would be used to buy agricultural inputs."

a1843.speaker: Officials of the Ministry of Trade & Regional Integration and the Ethiopian Trading Businesses Corporation
a1843.name: Officials of the Ministry of Trade & Regional Integration and the Ethiopian Trading Businesses Corporation
a1843.speech: Have declined to comment on this story.

a1843.speaker: Ahmed Shide, Minister of Finance
a1843.name: Ahmed Shide
a1843.title: Minister of Finance
a1843.speech: Hoped to see the country generate 200 million dollars from its first wheat export.

a1843.speaker: World Bank
a1843.name: World Bank
a1843.speech: Estimated Ethiopia's average fertiliser use at over 36Kgs per hectare.

a1843.speaker: World Food Program (WFP)
a1843.name: World Food Program (WFP)
a1843.speech: Reveals that more than 20 million people require food assistance, of which 7.9 million are under productive safety net programs.

a1843.speaker: Esayas Lemma, head of the crop development directorate under the Ministry of Agriculture
a1843.name: Esayas Lemma
a1843.title: head of the crop development directorate under the Ministry of Agriculture
a1843.speech: On officials offering aid organisations the option of buying wheat from the domestic "surplus" with foreign currency: "They can source it from the local market."

a1843.speaker: Esayas Lemma, head of the crop development directorate under the Ministry of Agriculture
a1843.name: Esayas Lemma
a1843.title: head of the crop development directorate under the Ministry of Agriculture
a1843.speech: Attributed the boost in demand to a change in lifestyle and urbanisation, and said most farmers consume 60pc of what they produce during the Meher season.

a1843.speaker: Adane Tufa, agricultural economist
a1843.name: Adane Tufa
a1843.title: agricultural economist
a1843.speech: Is one of the experts who, while applauding the efforts to become self-sufficient in wheat, question the wisdom of exporting wheat before ensuring local demands are fully covered; he believes the market reflects the gap in the wheat supply chain.

a1843.speaker: A macroeconomist requesting anonymity
a1843.name: A macroeconomist requesting anonymity
a1843.speech: Said that export should not be a priority in a country where inflation has diminished household incomes. He argued the country would not be competitive in the international market without lowering its price, noting top wheat-exporting countries like Ukraine compete in the global market with lower prices as they do not import agricultural inputs like fertiliser.

a1843.speaker: Netsanet Tesfaye, corporate communications manager, Ethiopian Commodity Exchange (ECX)
a1843.name: Netsanet Tesfaye
a1843.title: corporate communications manager, Ethiopian Commodity Exchange (ECX)
a1843.speech: Said the plan forwarded by the federal and regional authorities to export wheat to neighbouring markets is separate from the ECX.

a2025.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a2025.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a2025.speech: Gave a brief reminder of the objectives of the Global Compact for Migration at the start of the workshop.

a2025.speaker: Said Nouh Hassan, Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a2025.name: Said Nouh Hassan
a2025.title: Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a2025.speech: "It is with great pleasure that I welcome you today to the People's Palace for this important workshop presenting the work on the budgeted roadmap of the national migration strategy, as well as its monitoring and evaluation plan. At a time when the challenges linked to migration are at the heart of the government's discussions, the presentation of these tools or instruments such as the budgeted roadmap and its monitoring and evaluation plan comes at just the right moment to equip government institutions in the effective coordination of activities and of the financing required at national level with all stakeholders. I congratulate the BCNM, which has succeeded in coordinating the efforts of several partners, including IOM, GIZ and the company Kaizen, to achieve a synergy of results. This collaboration testifies to our determination to deal with the migration question in a proactive and effective manner." ; "In our approach to migration governance and management, it is essential to involve all stakeholders in order to guarantee an inclusive and equitable approach. The roadmap we are presenting today, along with its monitoring and evaluation plan, will constitute a solid foundation for our actions in the years to come."

a2025.speaker: Said Nouh Hassan, Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a2025.name: Said Nouh Hassan
a2025.title: Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a2025.speech: "However, it should be noted that there is a major obstacle to the success of our migration strategy: the glaring lack of funds. Our efforts to develop and implement an effective migration policy are constantly hampered by insufficient financial resources. This deficit limits our capacity to implement essential programmes that support the integration and management of migrants, thus affecting our ability to achieve the objectives of the Global Compact for Migration effectively. That is why I make an appeal to all the partners present to accompany us in the implementation of this roadmap. By uniting our efforts, we will be able to achieve the ambitious objectives of the Global Compact for Migration and move our country forward towards a better future for all."

a2025.speaker: Workshop participants (recommendation)
a2025.name: Workshop participants (recommendation)
a2025.speech: It was recommended to strengthen collaboration in a coherent and sustained manner in order to overcome the financial and logistical challenges, and to progress towards a future in which migration is managed equitably and beneficially for all.

a2037.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a2037.name: Nangolo Mbumba
a2037.title: President of Namibia
a2037.speech: Says the work of former US President Jimmy Carter left a permanent footprint in the annals of history, and in a statement said humanity has lost a champion for democracy and rights of the oppressed people of the world: "As a people who were occupied by the racist Apartheid Regime of South Africa, President Carter will be remembered for his commitment to human rights and the civil rights movement in the United States of America, which led to the adoption of progressive US policies in favour of independence across the globe. In that vein, the Namibian people will not only recall the exceptional humanitarian work of former President Carter in Africa and elsewhere, but will also recall his foreign policy which supported the right of Africa and the Namibian people to self-determination" ; extended condolences to the Carter family and the people of the USA.

a2064.speaker: Ewurabena Yanyi-Akofur, Country Director, WaterAid Ghana
a2064.name: Ewurabena Yanyi-Akofur
a2064.title: Country Director, WaterAid Ghana
a2064.speech: Said the ENWASH project aims to address critical gaps in WASH services, particularly in rural areas where access remained unequal; said in Ghana, while 68 per cent of health facilities had access to safe water, significant disparities persisted, adding, “Many facilities still rely on community boreholes or have no access to sanitation services at all”; expressed worry that this situation posed serious risks to maternal and child health and said that inadequate WASH services had been linked to maternal deaths and stagnant neonatal mortality rates; said stakeholders must ensure that facilities, especially maternity units, have access to clean water, proper sanitation and hygiene services, and that access to clean water, sanitation and proper waste disposal were fundamental to the health and safety of health workers and patients ; “As we hand over these facilities, we urge the health directorate and the district assembly to ensure the proper management and maintenance, as access to WASH services is a shared responsibility.”

a2064.speaker: Dr Samuel K. Boagye-Boateng, Regional Director of Health Services, Upper East Region
a2064.name: Dr Samuel K. Boagye-Boateng
a2064.title: Regional Director of Health Services, Upper East Region
a2064.speech: Said the availability of water was essential to health care delivery and expressed gratitude to WaterAid Ghana for the timely support: “As a directorate, we do appreciate the intervention by the organisation, as it would go a long way to enhance the provision of health services and improve the health needs of the people as well” ; urged the community members to jealously guard the project and maintain it as well, to motivate WaterAid Ghana to undertake similar projects in other communities.

a2064.speaker: Issaka Anabida, District Chief Executive for Tempane
a2064.name: Issaka Anabida
a2064.title: District Chief Executive for Tempane
a2064.speech: Commended the collaborative efforts between the community, the health directorate and WaterAid towards the execution of the project for their mutual benefit.

a2064.speaker: Cosmos Atowaje Minyilla, Bawku West District Director of Health Services
a2064.name: Cosmos Atowaje Minyilla
a2064.title: Bawku West District Director of Health Services
a2064.speech: Said the provision of the water facility would not only make the provision of healthcare easier but would improve the health needs of the people.

a2064.speaker: Abubakar Amoah Duut, Chief of Kongo
a2064.name: Abubakar Amoah Duut
a2064.title: Chief of Kongo
a2064.speech: Pleaded with the government to consider upgrading the facility to a health centre to serve the growing population in the community, indicating that the CHPS compound was too small and that the long queues at the facility continued to force the residents to seek medical care at nearby health facilities; he further commended the benefactors for providing the community with a potable water system.

a2064.speaker: Godfred Teye Anyorgbor, health officer in charge of the CHPS compound
a2064.name: Godfred Teye Anyorgbor
a2064.title: health officer in charge of the CHPS compound
a2064.speech: Said in an interview that hitherto, the provision of health services in the absence of water was very challenging for the workers, but stated that with the intervention by WaterAid Ghana water was now readily available to facilitate health delivery, saying, “In the absence of water at the facility, it was very difficult to run some laboratory services.”

a2064.speaker: Abigail Kanjeib, community member
a2064.name: Abigail Kanjeib
a2064.title: community member
a2064.speech: Lamented the suffering she went through when she delivered at the facility some few years ago and expressed delight that the water problem had been addressed: “I must tell you that it was an eyesore for the relatives of patients to bring water for it to be used by patients on admission at the health facility.”

a2064.speaker: Elizabeth Yendukua, resident
a2064.name: Elizabeth Yendukua
a2064.title: resident
a2064.speech: Thanked WaterAid Ghana and its sponsors for coming to their aid in their quest to access healthcare in the community.

a2132.speaker: Adegboyega Oyetola, Nigeria's Minister of Marine and Blue Economy
a2132.name: Adegboyega Oyetola
a2132.title: Nigeria's Minister of Marine and Blue Economy
a2132.speech: Said during the meeting with the Chinese Ambassador that Nigeria's vast maritime endowments included its 853 kilometers of coastline along the Atlantic Ocean and over 10,000 kilometers of inland waterways, and emphasised that Nigeria's maritime domain holds immense potential for shipping, port operations, fisheries, renewable ocean energy, marine tourism, and coastal infrastructure development. ; "Our ministry is determined to create the right framework for investment and partnership, and we believe that Nigeria has a lot to learn from China's marine and blue economy development model." ; "Nigeria's marine and blue economy holds tremendous opportunities for investors, and with China's cooperation, we are confident of unlocking this potential for the benefit of our people."

a2132.speaker: Yu Dunhai, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a2132.name: Yu Dunhai
a2132.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a2132.speech: Lauded Nigeria's vast maritime endowment and reaffirmed China's readiness to support Nigeria in harnessing its marine and blue economy potential. ; Highlighted the Lekki Deep Seaport, constructed by China Harbour Engineering Company, as a shining example of Sino-Nigerian collaboration, saying the project has created thousands of direct and indirect jobs, eased congestion at Lagos ports, and positioned Nigeria as a key maritime hub in West and Central Africa.

a2132.speaker: Yu Dunhai, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a2132.name: Yu Dunhai
a2132.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria
a2132.speech: Disclosed that an agreement is in the works for the export of Nigerian aquacultural products to China, which will open new markets for local producers and strengthen food trade ties between the two nations.

a2145.speaker: Institute for Security Studies (data modelling)
a2145.name: Institute for Security Studies (data modelling)
a2145.speech: Projects catastrophic outcomes: 5.7 million additional Africans will fall into extreme poverty (<$2.15/day) by 2026 if Trump's administration succeeds in its aid-reduction ambition.

a2145.speaker: John Mearsheimer, realist scholar
a2145.name: John Mearsheimer
a2145.title: realist scholar
a2145.speech: Asserted that "great powers always act in ways that maximize their relative power advantage."

a2145.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a2145.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a2145.speech: Announced the closure of its office in South Africa following the Trump administration's recent foreign aid cuts; the agency will consolidate its southern and East Africa operations into a single regional office in Nairobi, Kenya, while shutting down its Johannesburg office, citing a worsening donor funding outlook that has necessitated an acceleration of a restructuring plan initiated in 2023.

a2145.speaker: Abdirahim Mohamed Hassan, independent researcher and author
a2145.name: Abdirahim Mohamed Hassan
a2145.title: independent researcher and author
a2145.speech: Argued that Trump's policies reinforce a realist worldview and have validated dependency theory's core critique that North-South aid architectures perpetuate extractive relationships, and that Africa must respond with strategic foresight by rethinking its dependency on external actors and strengthening intra-African trade, security collaboration and independent policymaking; he wrote that "as the ruins of USAID are cleared, the foundations for a self-reliant Africa must rise in their place."

a2242.speaker: SADC Extraordinary Summit communique
a2242.name: SADC Extraordinary Summit communique
a2242.speech: "The summit terminated the Mandate of SAMIDRC [Southern African Development Community Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo] and directed the commencement of a phased withdrawal of SAMIDRC troops from the DRC."

a2242.speaker: SADC Extraordinary Summit communique
a2242.name: SADC Extraordinary Summit communique
a2242.speech: Called for the protection and free movement of civilians who are seeking safety and for all parties to uphold international humanitarian principles, stop attacks on civilians' infrastructure and guarantee unhindered humanitarian access ; "[The] summit noted the increasing humanitarian needs in the DRC and called on the international community, including the United Nations (UN) and the African Union, to provide humanitarian assistance to the people of the DRC." ; the 16-member grouping further agreed that there is a need for dedication to addressing the ongoing conflict in the DRC and reaffirmed its commitment to supporting interventions aimed at bringing lasting peace and security in the Eastern DRC, in line with the Sadc Mutual Defence Pact of 2003.

a2242.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2242.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2242.title: President of Malawi
a2242.speech: Said the order to the Malawi Defence Force Commander to begin preparations for the withdrawal of troops was one way of honouring the declaration of a cease fire by warring parties there ; also said it was meant to pave the way for warring parties' planned negotiations towards lasting peace, a development he hoped would bring stability to the Sadc region.

a2242.speaker: United Nations
a2242.name: United Nations
a2242.speech: According to the UN, at least 900 people have been killed and 2,880 injured in recent fighting in and around Goma, DRC's largest eastern city, after it was seized by rebels.

a2315.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2315.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2315.speech: urges Ethiopia to accelerate the birr depreciation and has also urged the authorities to closely monitor the impact of COVID-19 on financial stability; in its recently published COVID-19 related document, the IMF provided further support to stabilize the balance of payment and push the debt service and said that the government needs to increase the pace of depreciation: "Increasing the pace of depreciation would help reduce real overvaluation and act as a shock absorber during the crisis (COVID 19)," the IMF document said.

a2315.speaker: Ethiopian authorities/government (as reported in the IMF document)
a2315.name: Ethiopian authorities/government (as reported in the IMF document)
a2315.speech: said it will accelerate the birr depreciation with caution; the authorities underscored continued commitment to closing the gap with the parallel rate to eventually move to a market-clearing exchange rate but signaled a need to continue moving with caution ; the government remains committed to the objectives of the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) and Extended Financing Facility (EFF) arrangements that have been supporting Ethiopia’s economic reform program since December 2019, and the authorities underscored that they will continue to further the reform agenda ; "The government officials has highlighted their commitment to gradually ending financial repression by increasing T-bill issuances, ceasing new National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) financing to the Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) in June, and gradually reducing direct NBE advances to the government." ; "They also remain committed to implementing the FX roadmap to be finalized by end-April... to lay the groundwork for an eventual move to a market-clearing exchange rate."

a2315.speaker: Ethiopian government
a2315.name: Ethiopian government
a2315.speech: disclosed that it will arrange the exchange rate policy and indicated that the possibility of market based exchange rate might be introduced.

a2315.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2315.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2315.speech: recommended the government to closely follow the financial conditions at banks that are getting support from the central bank to stabilize their liquidity in relation with the coronavirus: "The measure (providing the 15 billion birr) aimed at addressing tight liquidity conditions that had arisen prior to COVID-19 and aids banks in repaying some of the 1 month loans previously provided through the Individual Bank Lending Facility-introduced in February-for the same purpose," IMF said ; supported the decision to build adequate liquidity buffers but emphasized the need to ensure that NBE lending to the CBE reflects the terms available to private banks and avoids implicit solvency support ; "NBE has appropriately provided liquidity to banks to maintain financial stability. Once the crisis abates, monetary policy will need to be tightened significantly to achieve the single-digit inflation objective. Strong efforts are needed to address the real overvaluation of the exchange rate, allowing the exchange rate to act as a shock absorber," IMF said.

a2315.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2315.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2315.speech: recommended close monitoring of liquidity positions, loan-to-deposit ratios, and asset quality: "In particular, there is an urgent need to step up monitoring of deposits and bank liquidity, as well as frequent supervisory review and reassessment of banks’ loan portfolios during the crisis," it said; it also emphasized the need to consider policy options to deal with potential further bank liquidity shortages, such as strengthening the framework for emergency lending and adjusting reserve requirements.

a2315.speaker: Joint World Bank–IMF Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA)
a2315.name: Joint World Bank–IMF Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA)
a2315.speech: shows that debt is sustainable: "However, liquidity pressures to service external debt have increased, the room to absorb shocks is now smaller than at program approval due to lower export projections, and a large or more persistent impact of the COVID-19 shock than presently assumed could further worsen the outlook," it said ; on the domestic front, public debt remains vulnerable to contingent liability shocks, including those stemming from public banks: "Despite severe losses due to COVID-19, Ethiopian Airlines intends to continue servicing its debt and does not have plans to seek government support."

a2422.speaker: Dr Yemi Kale, Chief Economist of Afreximbank
a2422.name: Dr Yemi Kale
a2422.title: Chief Economist of Afreximbank
a2422.speech: Presented the African Trade Report 2025, entitled "African Trade in a Shifting Global Financial Architecture", to the assembly, drawing up a rigorous assessment of African trade in a global context marked by geopolitical fragmentation, the rise of protectionism and the redefinition of international economic rules.

a2422.speaker: Afreximbank African Trade Report 2025
a2422.name: Afreximbank African Trade Report 2025
a2422.speech: Highlights a significant rebound in the continent's trade, which reached $1,527 billion, up 13.9% compared with 2023, with intra-African trade growing 12.4% to $220.3 billion, while structural challenges remain: an annual trade finance gap estimated at $100 billion, persistent dependence on raw materials, weak export diversification and intra-African trade still representing only 14.4% of total trade; it highlights major instruments of transformation (AfCFTA, PAPSS, AAMFI) and calls for urgent reform of the global financial system, denouncing the biases of credit ratings and the Basel IV rules as penalising for African banks, and presents the African Union's entry into the G20 as a strategic opportunity to claim a fair place in global economic governance.

a2422.speaker: Prof. Benedict Oramah, President of Afreximbank
a2422.name: Prof. Benedict Oramah
a2422.title: President of Afreximbank
a2422.speech: Called for the current crises to be turned into a catalyst for a new era: "Africa must not be marginalised by the fragmentation of the world, but must make it a springboard towards a more integrated, resilient and autonomous economy."

a2557.speaker: Yulia Svyrydenko, First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Economy of Ukraine (Facebook post)
a2557.name: Yulia Svyrydenko
a2557.title: First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Economy of Ukraine (Facebook post)
a2557.speech: Reported that Washington and Kyiv had signed a memorandum of intent with a view to an agreement on Ukrainian mineral resources/rare earths, noting that the document provides for “the creation of an Investment Fund for the recovery of Ukraine” and will contribute to the modernisation of the country's infrastructure: “An agreement along these lines will offer opportunities for significant investment, a modernisation of infrastructure and mutually beneficial cooperation between Ukraine and the United States: it is to this end that our teams are working on this document.”

a2557.speaker: Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary
a2557.name: Scott Bessent
a2557.title: US Treasury Secretary
a2557.speech: “That is, in substance, what had previously been agreed,” he assured the press on 17 April.

a2557.speaker: Yaroslav Zhelezniak, deputy in the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament)
a2557.name: Yaroslav Zhelezniak
a2557.title: deputy in the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament)
a2557.speech: Indicated that the new draft minerals agreement was very unfavourable to Kyiv and could increase Ukraine's dependence on the United States.

a2557.speaker: Memorandum (signed document)
a2557.name: Memorandum (signed document)
a2557.speech: According to the memorandum, Ukrainian Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal will travel to Washington next week to meet the US Treasury Secretary and discuss the creation of an Investment Fund.

a2599.speaker: Inspector Simon Chazovachiyi, Mashonaland East provincial police spokesperson
a2599.name: Inspector Simon Chazovachiyi
a2599.title: Mashonaland East provincial police spokesperson
a2599.speech: Confirmed the incident and said the victim was referred to Parirenyatwa Hospital for a medical examination and that investigations are in progress.

a2599.speaker: Suspected armed robber (unnamed)
a2599.name: Suspected armed robber (unnamed)
a2599.speech: Reportedly quizzed the victim why she did not make a payment to be on the mountain, saying the place was a protected place under the National Museums and Monuments of Zimbabwe; claimed to be part of the security personnel assigned to monitor movements on the mountain and told the victim that she was under arrest, and threatened to kill her if she refused to comply with his orders.

a2781.speaker: Volker Türk, United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2781.name: Volker Türk
a2781.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2781.speech: Warns that despite the peace agreements signed in Doha and Washington, attacks against civilians are multiplying in eastern Congo ; expressed on Wednesday 6 August his deep concern at the resurgence of attacks against civilian populations in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, a deterioration that comes paradoxically at a time when several peace agreements have recently been concluded, notably in Doha and Washington.

a2781.speaker: United Nations (statistics)
a2781.name: United Nations (statistics)
a2781.speech: The statistics released by the UN paint a particularly bleak picture: from 9 to 21 July, no fewer than 319 civilians lost their lives in four villages in Rutshuru territory, victims of attacks carried out by the M23 movement; among these victims were 48 women and 19 children, mainly farmers deliberately targeted.

a2781.speaker: Reports (unattributed reports cited)
a2781.name: Reports (unattributed reports cited)
a2781.speech: Reports also state that gang rapes took place, adding to the horror of this humanitarian crisis.

a2781.speaker: Volker Türk, United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2781.name: Volker Türk
a2781.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2781.speech: Directly calls on the actors in the conflict, urging them to respect their obligations to protect civilians and international humanitarian law; he asks in particular the signatories of the Doha and Washington agreements to give concrete form to their commitments in order to definitively break the cycles of violence affecting the region.

a2781.speaker: United States Embassy in Kinshasa
a2781.name: United States Embassy in Kinshasa
a2781.speech: Made public the agreement, which establishes a legally binding framework covering the political, security, humanitarian and economic dimensions of the conflict.

a2781.speaker: American authorities
a2781.name: American authorities
a2781.speech: According to the American authorities, these advances pave the way for a future Heads of State Summit intended to consolidate peace and development in the Great Lakes region.

a2781.speaker: Volker Türk, United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2781.name: Volker Türk
a2781.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2781.speech: As the High Commissioner's alert underlines, local populations continue to live in "deep uncertainty" in the absence of tangible progress on the ground.

a2840.speaker: Belmiro Casimiro, administrator of the district of Ancuabe, Cabo Delgado
a2840.name: Belmiro Casimiro
a2840.title: administrator of the district of Ancuabe, Cabo Delgado
a2840.speech: warned of the existence of informants for rebel groups among communities affected by armed attacks: "The other challenge we have identified in our district is the issue of informants for the terrorists. In our communities, there are always some individuals who serve as links with the terrorists. It is urgent for the government, with the involvement of all communities, to ensure that these informants understand that they are destroying the social fabric of our economy and of our district of Ancuabe."

a2840.speaker: Belmiro Casimiro, administrator of the district of Ancuabe, Cabo Delgado
a2840.name: Belmiro Casimiro
a2840.title: administrator of the district of Ancuabe, Cabo Delgado
a2840.speech: said the armed conflict has been slowing the district's development, which has been "repeatedly affected" by the insurgency: "Our development is being hindered by terrorism. We have been cyclically affected by the consequences of this evil, which is a major challenge not only for our district but also for our Government of Mozambique as a whole."

a2840.speaker: Jorge Corio, national director of Criminalistics at SERNIC
a2840.name: Jorge Corio
a2840.title: national director of Criminalistics at SERNIC
a2840.speech: said there were "some shortcomings in the collection of evidence" for analysis, reiterating the need to train Mozambican forces in this area: "As you know, when a crime occurs, an attack on a village or a town, there are always traces, evidence that is useful for investigation."

a2840.speaker: Previous official data
a2840.name: Previous official data
a2840.speech: According to previous official data, by the end of July, attacks by these groups had already caused more than 57,000 displacements in the district of Chiure, in the south of Cabo Delgado province.

a2840.speaker: United Nations (data)
a2840.name: United Nations (data)
a2840.speech: According to United Nations data, between 19 and 26 September 2025, the escalation of attacks and the insecurity caused by armed groups in Cabo Delgado led to around 22,000 people being displaced in the districts of Balama, Mocimboa da Praia and Nangade.

a2840.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a2840.name: Daniel Chapo
a2840.title: Mozambican President
a2840.speech: said on 25 September that security in Cabo Delgado had improved but that the terrorist threat remained, calling on the Mozambican Defence Armed Forces (FADM) to devise "strategies to eliminate" these insurgent groups.

a2840.speaker: Published data
a2840.name: Published data
a2840.speech: According to published data, in 2024 alone at least 349 people were killed in attacks in northern Mozambique, most of them claimed by the extremist group Islamic State, representing a 36 per cent increase compared with the previous year.

a2840.speaker: Government of Mozambique (figures)
a2840.name: Government of Mozambique (figures)
a2840.speech: According to government figures, two million Mozambicans are facing food insecurity, of whom 148,000 require "urgent humanitarian assistance."

a2963.speaker: Virginia Gamba, acting Special Adviser of the UN Secretary-General on the Prevention of Genocide
a2963.name: Virginia Gamba
a2963.title: acting Special Adviser of the UN Secretary-General on the Prevention of Genocide
a2963.speech: Warned on Monday that the risk of genocide, as well as of war crimes and crimes against humanity, remains “very high” in Sudan; before the Human Rights Council she denounced the persistent ethnic attacks in Sudan, notably targeting the Zaghawa, Masalit and Fur communities in the Darfur and Kordofan regions.

a2963.speaker: Virginia Gamba, acting Special Adviser of the UN Secretary-General on the Prevention of Genocide
a2963.name: Virginia Gamba
a2963.title: acting Special Adviser of the UN Secretary-General on the Prevention of Genocide
a2963.speech: Said she was also alarmed by the situation in Gaza, evoking “staggering and unacceptable civilian suffering”; she denounced the Israeli military campaign, the source of heavy human losses and massive destruction, while calling for an immediate ceasefire, the release of the hostages and unimpeded access for humanitarian aid.

a2963.speaker: Virginia Gamba, acting Special Adviser of the UN Secretary-General on the Prevention of Genocide
a2963.name: Virginia Gamba
a2963.title: acting Special Adviser of the UN Secretary-General on the Prevention of Genocide
a2963.speech: In Africa, pointed to the ethnic violence in South Sudan, the repression of Fulani populations in the Sahel – notably in Burkina Faso – and the rise of hate speech in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, where fighting with the M23 armed group continues: “Ethnic violence, serious human rights violations and impunity are fuelling a dangerous cycle in several regions of the world,” she warned, urging the international community to take immediate action.

a2976.speaker: Russel Msiska, Executive Director of Beyond Our Hearts Foundation
a2976.name: Russel Msiska
a2976.title: Executive Director of Beyond Our Hearts Foundation
a2976.speech: Said the maize will help the hunger-stricken families survive during these difficult times.

a2976.speaker: Group Village Headman Malunda
a2976.name: Group Village Headman Malunda
a2976.speech: Advised the beneficiaries not to sell the maize, emphasizing its importance in helping them survive the current food shortages: “This maize is a lifeline for your families, and it’s crucial that you use it wisely.”

a2976.speaker: Dick Zangwa, Chairperson for the Area Development Committee
a2976.name: Dick Zangwa
a2976.title: Chairperson for the Area Development Committee
a2976.speech: Described the donation as timely: “Many households in our area did not harvest enough due to the effects of climate change, so this donation is a much-needed relief” ; He called on other organizations to emulate the gesture, highlighting the ongoing need for support in the area.

a2976.speaker: Maggie Mikatere, beneficiary from Malunda village
a2976.name: Maggie Mikatere
a2976.title: beneficiary from Malunda village
a2976.speech: Expressed gratitude for the donation: “The 50kg bag of maize will help my family survive for weeks” ; Emphasized that the hunger situation in the area requires a multisectoral approach to address the root causes of food insecurity.

a3080.speaker: Chinese military officials
a3080.name: Chinese military officials
a3080.speech: Said at a news conference on Wednesday that hundreds of People’s Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft, including fighter jets and bombers, as well as ground forces with the latest military equipment, will be featured in the parade.

a3080.speaker: Xinhua, China’s official news agency
a3080.name: Xinhua
a3080.title: China’s official news agency
a3080.speech: Said the military parade and “joint armament formations... will be organised in a manner reflecting their functions in real combat”, and will include air, land and sea combat groups.

a3080.speaker: Global Times, China’s state-affiliated media outlet
a3080.name: Global Times
a3080.title: China’s state-affiliated media outlet
a3080.speech: “The military parade will feature new fourth-generation equipment as the core, including advanced tanks, carrier-based aircraft and fighter jets, organised into operational modules to demonstrate Chinese military’s system-based combat capability” ; “All the weaponry and equipment on display in this military parade are domestically produced active-duty main battle equipment. This event showcases a concentrated display of the new generation of weaponry and equipment of the Chinese military.”

a3080.speaker: Foreign military attaches and security analysts (anonymous)
a3080.name: Foreign military attaches and security analysts (anonymous)
