a5241.speech: said on the challenge of the taxpayer identification number (TIN), that consultants are asked for business licences and TIN numbers as a requirement for being granted a practising licence, which causes many applications to fail, because the authorities that issue business licences and TINs ask for practising licences in order to satisfy themselves that the applicant has the proper qualifications ; "At TEEA we requested that amendments be made to the 2021 environmental management regulations on this matter."

a5241.speaker: Emmanuel Hanai, Chairman of the Tanzania Environmental Experts Association (TEEA)
a5241.name: Emmanuel Hanai
a5241.title: Chairman of the Tanzania Environmental Experts Association (TEEA)
a5241.speech: said on the challenge of delays in land title deeds, that titles have been delaying the completion of EIAs in many projects and causing some investors to cancel and do something else; he said this arises because investors who have borrowed are required to begin repaying loans, and asked that the authorities give the council director the mandate to confirm to NEMC that an area has been zoned for the relevant use; he said documents come from the director but are validated by the commissioner and the registrar of titles.

a5241.speaker: Christina Mndeme, Deputy Permanent Secretary in the Vice-President's Office (Union and Environment)
a5241.name: Christina Mndeme
a5241.title: Deputy Permanent Secretary in the Vice-President's Office (Union and Environment)
a5241.speech: responding, said she had heard their challenges and that the Vice-President's Office would continue to work on those challenges in order to improve their performance ; "I promise you that your work will be easier than it was yesterday. On the regulatory challenges, I call on TEEA and NEMC to cooperate in reviewing those regulations so as to identify the areas that create challenges in the work of environmental consultants."

a5340.speaker: John Kapito, CAMA (Consumers Association of Malawi) Executive Director
a5340.name: John Kapito
a5340.title: CAMA (Consumers Association of Malawi) Executive Director
a5340.speech: Says in the petition that the questions have been developed and inspired by the aspiring candidates' "brilliant manifesto" that they have unveiled, and adds that the purpose of the questions is for the candidates to expand and provide clarity especially on how the resources will be generated and support the many good outcomes of their manifestos.

a5340.speaker: Consumers Association of Malawi (CAMA) (petition to presidential aspirants)
a5340.name: Consumers Association of Malawi (CAMA) (petition to presidential aspirants)
a5340.speech: Has asked the September 16 presidential election aspirants to clearly spell out how resources will be generated to successfully implement their manifestos, expecting responses by August 30 ; "Our role is to encourage and mobilise consumers throughout the country on how your manifesto and subsequent policies will protect the interests of consumers. Your responses will go a long way in strengthening your campaign messages." ; urges all political parties and their aspirants "to provide comprehensive socio-economic recovery plans for the struggling economy" with "short, intermediate and long-term interventions that will catalyse economic growth" ; "The expectation that political promises alone will suffice to sway votes in the upcoming election continues to dwindle for potential voters. Malawians are seeking far more than mere strategies. Malawians want tangible, impactful and measurable interventions in order to continue believing that the leaders of today can initiate the process towards the nation achieving the MW2063 goals. Malawians acknowledge the brilliance of all potential proposals - but they are seeking clear and visionary leaders who comprehend the current economic and social challenges they face. Leaders who are willing to provide practical, research-based, result oriented interventions. They are eager to find out what you can do that other candidates cannot do and have not done before." ; poses questions including, on Foreign Aid: "Considering that there is a continued geopolitical shift towards nationalist sentiments that have led many nations to rethink their aid positions; what strategies will your administration employ to replace the funding gaps left behind by aid withdraw and further reduce aid dependence?" and, on Development Expenditure: "Considering that the development budget has predominantly been foreign funded; what methods have you developed to reverse the balance towards self-funded development?" ; "CAMA believes that many expectations are born from desperation. Hope indeed sprouts out of the ashes of despair. The nation is edging towards a momentous election on September 16, 2025. Do not fall into the temptation to sway votes by selling false promises. Go forth and speak only political truth that will unite and uplift the nation from the socio-economic quagmire and set us back on the path to achieving the beautiful vision of MW2063 Goals."

a5364.speaker: Davie Mlose, Zomba City Council director of administration
a5364.name: Davie Mlose
a5364.title: Zomba City Council director of administration
a5364.speech: Has warned Cyclone Jude survivors in Zomba against misusing resources they receive from well-wishers; said relief funds from non-governmental organisations (NGOs) are meant to help survivors get back to their feet and rebuild their homes; said failure to utilise the money will push more people into poverty. “Invest the funds in sustainable activities that can restore your previous livelihoods.”

a5364.speaker: Blessings Mlowoka, Self Help Africa humanitarian committee coordinator
a5364.name: Blessings Mlowoka
a5364.title: Self Help Africa humanitarian committee coordinator
a5364.speech: Said the funds are meant to help households build their resilience against climate shocks. “The funds should boost the survivors’ capacities and buy utensils and repair their houses. Stable families are essential to development.”

a5364.speaker: Esinala Kumtembwe, a beneficiary from Mpunga Township
a5364.name: Esinala Kumtembwe
a5364.title: a beneficiary from Mpunga Township
a5364.speech: Said part of her house collapsed and destroyed utensils and foodstuffs. “I will, therefore, use the funds for its intended purpose, to repair my house and buy utensils.”

a5364.speaker: Esinala Kumtembwe, a beneficiary from Mpunga Township
a5364.name: Esinala Kumtembwe
a5364.title: a beneficiary from Mpunga Township
a5364.speech: Appealed to other well-wishers to emulate the example set by Self Help Africa and reach out to the survivors with humanitarian assistance.

a5374.speaker: Mohamud Ma'alin, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Authority (SoDMA)
a5374.name: Mohamud Ma'alin
a5374.title: Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Authority (SoDMA)
a5374.speech: Opened the meeting by emphasizing the importance of engaging religious scholars and the community in SoDMA's decision-making processes; highlighted that since its inception in 2022, SoDMA has consistently valued the insights of religious scholars; also addressed the current vulnerabilities caused by the extremist group Al-Shabaab, which has disrupted farming and displaced hundreds of thousands, exacerbating the humanitarian crisis.

a5374.speaker: Abdirahman, Member of Parliament
a5374.name: Abdirahman
a5374.title: Member of Parliament
a5374.speech: Commended SoDMA's efforts, noting the significant benefits that have accrued to the population since the agency's re-establishment two years ago; stressed the importance of providing security as a prerequisite to effective humanitarian assistance.

a5374.speaker: Ali Hagi Dahir, Chair of the Parliamentary Committee on Justice and Religious Affairs
a5374.name: Ali Hagi Dahir
a5374.title: Chair of the Parliamentary Committee on Justice and Religious Affairs
a5374.speech: Emphasized Somalia's rich agricultural potential and urged religious leaders to raise awareness about farming; called on SoDMA to facilitate agricultural activities to enhance self-sufficiency.

a5374.speaker: Sheikh Ali Wajis, prominent religious leader
a5374.name: Sheikh Ali Wajis
a5374.title: prominent religious leader
a5374.speech: Reinforced the need for humanitarian efforts, suggesting the imposition of a 2% salary contribution for such causes; proposed that business communities should also pledge regular contributions and recommended that the President be accompanied by humanitarian teams, led by SoDMA, during official visits; also advocated for relocating IDP camps from the capital to allow displaced individuals to return home.

a5374.speaker: Faduma Adle, Chair of Somali Women Religious Scholars
a5374.name: Faduma Adle
a5374.title: Chair of Somali Women Religious Scholars
a5374.speech: Advocated for the integration of religious leaders into SoDMA's framework, suggesting the establishment of a dedicated department for them.

a5430.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a5430.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a5430.title: Ukrainian President
a5430.speech: Judged on Thursday that Donald Trump’s “unpredictability” could help bring an end to the war in Ukraine: “Trump can be decisive (...) in this war. He can help us stop (Vladimir) Putin. He is very strong and unpredictable,” he said in a televised interview, saying the U.S. president-elect “really wants to end the war” ; “I would really like this unpredictability of President Trump to apply to Russia.”

a5430.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a5430.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a5430.title: Ukrainian President
a5430.speech: Judged on Thursday that any security guarantee to Ukraine not involving the United States would be “weak guarantees”, and that a possible European military contingent deployed in Ukraine must not replace his country’s NATO membership: “We would not want there to be only one or two countries for this initiative. This initiative absolutely must go in the direction of NATO. That does not mean that the deployment of European forces excludes a future within NATO.”

a5430.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a5430.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a5430.title: Ukrainian President
a5430.speech: Acknowledged that the situation on the eastern front is “really very difficult” and that Ukrainian troops “are tired”, notably because of a “lack of reserves and rotation” of personnel.

a5444.speaker: Gisèle Takalea, Vice-President of a network of associations fighting HIV and other diseases
a5444.name: Gisèle Takalea
a5444.title: Vice-President of a network of associations fighting HIV and other diseases
a5444.speech: Declared on Tuesday at a press conference: “The freezing of foreign aid by the United States government represents a serious threat to public health in Côte d'Ivoire.”

a5444.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5444.name: Donald Trump
a5444.title: US President
a5444.speech: Ordered, shortly after his inauguration in January, the suspension of 92% of the funding of overseas programmes by the US development agency (USAID).

a5585.speaker: Tina Salama, spokesperson for Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi
a5585.name: Tina Salama
a5585.title: spokesperson for Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi
a5585.speech: Reading the presidential order on national television on Tuesday 1 April 2025, announced that the death sentences of Marcel Malanga, Benjamin Zalman and Taylor Thompson had been commuted to life imprisonment.

a5585.speaker: Sylva Mbikay, one of the lawyers for Marcel Malanga
a5585.name: Sylva Mbikay
a5585.title: one of the lawyers for Marcel Malanga
a5585.speech: Explains that the next step concerns their extradition to the United States: “When a defendant is sentenced to death, the public prosecutor’s office must do everything possible for that sentence to be commuted to life imprisonment. These people have no family here in Congo. We will do everything in our power to demand their extradition to their country of origin, the United States of America, where they will be able to serve their sentence.”

a5585.speaker: Some observers
a5585.name: Some observers
a5585.speech: According to them, this presidential pardon granted by Kinshasa is a charm offensive aimed at preparing for negotiations with Washington in the framework of the mining and security agreement between the two states.

a5585.speaker: Christian Moleka, Dynamique des politologues (DYPOL)
a5585.name: Christian Moleka
a5585.title: Dynamique des politologues (DYPOL)
a5585.speech: Believes that “the fact that these are only Americans suggests that there may be a form of willingness to soften, or at least to create good conditions for negotiation, while at the same time removing an issue known to be contentious, which could anger the delegation and be a point of discord in the negotiation.”

a5781.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.speech: Announced today that 15 trucks that were to have distributed supplies on Thursday night to bakeries run by the UN agency in the south of the Gaza Strip were looted.

a5781.speaker: United Nations agencies
a5781.name: United Nations agencies
a5781.speech: Warned of the risk that catastrophic levels of hunger will again be recorded in the Gaza Strip and of the worsening health crisis in the occupied West Bank.

a5781.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.speech: Warned today that only four to five days of food remain in the stores of the Gaza Strip, the Palestinian enclave surrounded by the Israeli army following the attack carried out by Hamas against Israel.

a5781.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.speech: Warned today that millions of people in the Horn of Africa remain in a situation of “emerging famine,” amid a series of crises.

a5781.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.speech: Announced today the end of the suspension of its mission in Sudan in the face of the worsening crisis in the country due to the fighting between the army and the paramilitary group Rapid Support Forces.

a5781.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.speech: Announced today that it will be forced to suspend food aid, from next month and until January, to more than 100,000 displaced people in South Sudan, for lack of funding.

a5781.speaker: Norwegian Nobel Committee
a5781.name: Norwegian Nobel Committee
a5781.speech: Announced that the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the United Nations World Food Programme for its efforts to combat hunger and to improve [the conditions of] populations living in conflict zones.

a5781.speaker: An official of the World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.name: An official of the World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5781.speech: Said today that the truce period in Yemen allowed the UN, for the first time in six months, to send food to the south of the country.

a5781.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a5781.name: Government of Mozambique
a5781.speech: Indicated today that it intends to reduce chronic malnutrition in children aged zero to five from the current 43% to 35% in 2019, through the promotion of nutrient consumption and increased food production.

a5845.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Malawi Finance and Economic Planning Minister
a5845.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a5845.title: Malawi Finance and Economic Planning Minister
a5845.speech: Moved the motion enabling the House to conduct the Committee of Supply ; informed Parliament that additional funds had been allocated to key sectors, including the Ministry of Health, National Assembly operations, and infrastructure compensation under the Millennium Challenge Account top-up.

a5904.speaker: Oluwalade Demilade, debate finalist supporting the motion
a5904.name: Oluwalade Demilade
a5904.title: debate finalist supporting the motion
a5904.speech: “The top five fastest growing countries in the world in 2024 have all received hundreds of billions in financial aid. Foreign aid improves bi-lateral trades between the giver and receivers and the US is the largest giving economy which maintains top relations with giving states such as Ukraine, Israel and Ethiopia.”

a5904.speaker: Mary Uke, 15-year-old debate winner
a5904.name: Mary Uke
a5904.title: 15-year-old debate winner
a5904.speech: Responding, said: “Financial aid does not equate economic growth, other factors must be in place such as good governance and structure.” She added that foreign aid almost always only benefitted corporate city institutions instead of local and rural institutions.

a5941.speaker: Pentagon and State Department officials familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a5941.name: Pentagon and State Department officials familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a5941.speech: Said the new arms packages include more than 1800 MK84 2,000-pound bombs and 500 MK82 500-pound bombs; these officials talked with The Washington Post under the condition of anonymity because recent authorisations have not been made public.

a5941.speaker: Sources (unnamed)
a5941.name: Sources (unnamed)
a5941.speech: Claimed that the United States government under the leadership of President Joe Biden has approved the transfer of billions of dollars in bombs and fighter jets to Israel despite Washington's concerns about an anticipated military offensive in southern Gaza that could threaten the lives of hundreds of thousands of Palestinian civilians.

a5941.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a5941.name: White House official (anonymous)
a5941.speech: “We have continued to support Israel's right to defend itself. Conditioning aid has not been our policy.”

a5941.speaker: Some Democrats, including allies of President Biden
a5941.name: Some Democrats
a5941.title: including allies of President Biden
a5941.speech: Say the U.S. government has a responsibility to withhold weapons in the absence of an Israeli commitment to limit civilian casualties during a planned operation in Rafah, a final Hamas stronghold, and ease restrictions on humanitarian aid into the enclave, which is on the brink of famine.

a5941.speaker: Israeli government
a5941.name: Israeli government
a5941.speech: Declined to comment on the authorisations.

a5941.speaker: U.S. and Israeli officials
a5941.name: U.S. and Israeli officials
a5941.speech: Say four Hamas battalions remain in Rafah.

a5941.speaker: President Joe Biden
a5941.name: President Joe Biden
a5941.speech: Suggested that a scorched-earth invasion of the city along Gaza's border with Egypt would cross a “red line” for him ; requested that Netanyahu send a team of security officials to Washington this week to listen to U.S. proposals for limiting the bloodshed.

a5941.speaker: The White House
a5941.name: The White House
a5941.speech: Said Israeli officials have not allayed U.S. concerns about the impending operation in Rafah, but they agreed to reschedule the meeting in Washington.

a6001.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement on its official website)
a6001.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement on its official website)
a6001.speech: Announced that effective Friday, February 7, USAID will place all direct-hire personnel worldwide on administrative leave, and that for USAID staff stationed outside the United States the agency, in collaboration with local missions, is formulating a plan to arrange and fund return travel to the U.S. within 30 days.

a6001.speaker: U.S. Embassy (no response)
a6001.name: U.S. Embassy (no response)
a6001.speech: nbc News reached out to the U.S. Embassy to establish how many local jobs the closure of USAID will affect and how this closure will directly impact the work being done by the programme; the nbc will give an update once the embassy has responded.

a6234.speaker: Le Monde (French daily, quoted)
a6234.name: Le Monde (French daily
a6234.title: quoted)
a6234.speech: "The putschist soldiers in Guinea began to consolidate their power on Wednesday evening, 24 December, two days after the death of President Lansana Conte. Weapons in hand, they paraded in the afternoon through the centre of Conakry, where they were cheered by thousands of Guineans forming an enthusiastic crowd. 'Long live the new leader', 'long live the new Guinea', shouted the inhabitants who had invaded the Avenue de la Republique leading to the presidential palace in the afternoon."

a6234.speaker: Guinean crowds in Conakry (as reported by Le Monde)
a6234.name: Guinean crowds in Conakry (as reported by Le Monde)
a6234.speech: Shouted "Long live the new leader", "long live the new Guinea".

a6234.speaker: Captain Moussa Dadis Camara
a6234.name: Captain Moussa Dadis Camara
a6234.speech: Promised to establish democracy in the country, but spoke of free elections only in December 2010; he had also claimed in the press that he would not be a candidate, before apparently reversing his position.

a6234.speaker: Captain Moussa Dadis Camara (remarks reported by the website koaci.com)
a6234.name: Captain Moussa Dadis Camara (remarks reported by the website koaci.com)
a6234.speech: "For the moment, I do not know whether there were any deaths," he reportedly said a few hours after the killings, and later said he was sorry about what had happened.

a6234.speaker: Senegalese President Abdoulaye Wade
a6234.name: Senegalese President Abdoulaye Wade
a6234.speech: Gave barely veiled support to the Guinean junta a few weeks earlier, which may have encouraged the self-styled Guinean hero in his attitude.

a6345.speaker: Stacy Gilbert, former US State Department official, Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration
a6345.name: Stacy Gilbert
a6345.title: former US State Department official, Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration
a6345.speech: Said on Thursday her resignation was precipitated by an administration report to Congress that she said falsely stated Israel was not blocking humanitarian aid to Gaza, prompting her to resign in protest of US President Joe Biden's Israel policy. “There is so clearly a right and wrong, and what is in that report is wrong,” Gilbert said in an interview.

a6345.speaker: Stacy Gilbert, former US State Department official, Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration
a6345.name: Stacy Gilbert
a6345.title: former US State Department official, Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration
a6345.speech: Said she notified her office the day the State Department report was released that she would resign ; said the State Department removed subject matter experts from working on the report to Congress when the document was a rough draft about 10 days before it was due; she said the report was then edited by more senior officials; in contrast to the published version, the last draft she saw stated that Israel was blocking humanitarian assistance, Gilbert said.

a6345.speaker: United Nations and aid groups
a6345.name: United Nations and aid groups
a6345.speech: Have long complained of the dangers and obstacles to getting aid in and distributing it throughout Gaza.

a6345.speaker: Human rights groups and other critics
a6345.name: Human rights groups and other critics
a6345.speech: Have faulted the US for providing weapons to Israel and largely defending Israel's conduct.

a6345.speaker: US State Department report to Congress (46-page unclassified report)
a6345.name: US State Department report to Congress (46-page unclassified report)
a6345.speech: Among other conclusions, the report said that in the period after 7 October Israel “did not fully cooperate” with US and other efforts to get humanitarian aid into Gaza. But it said this did not amount to a breach of a US law that blocks the provision of arms to countries that restrict US humanitarian aid.

a6345.speaker: Vedant Patel, US State Department deputy spokesperson
a6345.name: Vedant Patel
a6345.title: US State Department deputy spokesperson
a6345.speech: Told reporters on Thursday that he would not comment on personnel issues but that the department welcomes diverse points of view. He said the administration stood by the report and continued to press the government of Israel to avoid harming civilians and urgently expand humanitarian access to Gaza. “We are not an administration that twists the facts, and allegations that we have are unfounded,” Patel said.

a6345.speaker: Israeli embassy in Washington
a6345.name: Israeli embassy in Washington
a6345.speech: Did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Gilbert's accusations.

a6345.speaker: Classified initial options memo (reported exclusively by Reuters in late April)
a6345.name: Classified initial options memo (reported exclusively by Reuters in late April)
a6345.speech: Informed US Secretary of State Antony Blinken Israel might be violating international humanitarian law.

a6345.speaker: Israeli tallies
a6345.name: Israeli tallies
a6345.speech: According to Israeli tallies, Hamas fighters who crossed from Gaza into southern Israel on 7 October 2023 killed 1 200 people and abducted more than 250.

a6352.speaker: Guinéenéews (interviewer, LY Abdoul)
a6352.name: Guinéenéews (interviewer
a6352.title: LY Abdoul)
a6352.speech: Asked: “Although you have been away from the country for some years, in your view and quite clearly, what is currently wrong in the culture sector, and have there been any advances since?” ; “Since Minister Bill de Sam was your artist, what practical advice had you given him?” ; “After this stage of Minister Bill de Sam, can you then describe the other one, which coincides with the appointment of Moussa Moise Sylla at the head of this department?” ; “Have there been any advances in this sector?” ; “Ambassadors of Guinea's African culture, today the Ballets Africains are a problem. How do you feel about it?” ; “The Ballets africains are undergoing a major transformation; were you involved?”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On the management of the Ministry of Culture under Minister Bill de Sam: “There was hope when Bill de Sam arrived at the head of this department. Honestly, and as an observation, together with Dyéssira Condé, for whom I have a religious respect, my advice was not listened to by that new team, and they were completely disconnected from reality... They shut themselves within four walls, and in my opinion, and one must dare to say it, that is what explains one of the causes of their failure. I was one of the first defenders of Bill de Sam when he was appointed to this post of minister... So he is a brother, who did not take the time to listen to my advice.” ; “That same Bill de Sam team had tried to strip us of the management of the Ballets africains de Guinée, in a deal proposed by young promoters whom I, Tidiane, had myself helped to obtain entry visas for Canada... So I keep that bad memory of that team.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On the advice he gave Bill de Sam: “I had nevertheless publicly supported that team, and it could have succeeded. I even advised holding conferences instead of shutting themselves away. That team was much more concerned with examining the legal texts than with time spent acting in the field. They were rather bureaucratic, ideological, and that weighed heavily on them... That is the sort of advice I gave my brother Bill de Sam. When you create a team, a clan, it becomes like show business, and that does not last.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On the current ministry under Moussa Moise Sylla and on François Bourouno: “Personally, I appreciate the dynamism that the latter brought to the sector. I confirm today that Mr. François Bourouno is the best, most competent official I have known in the history of this ministry, and since General Mamady Doumbouya came to power.” ; “Within this ministry, we have nothing but enemies at the level of the minister's office, and I do not need to name names... When public servants treat State affairs as private obligations, I regret such behaviour, and I am obliged to denounce such acts, which tend to personalise State affairs.” ; “It was he who came and settled the crisis that arose between us and Bill de Sam's team. He considered us, respected us, and, cards on the table, we obtained the contract for the Ballets africains de Guinée.” ; “And it was in the meantime that our brother Moussa Moise was appointed. I welcome his arrival, although he does not come from the sector; nevertheless, I am observing for the time being what his vision is.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On whether there have been advances in the sector: “There are people in that office who do not want to see, nor accept, a project managed or led by Tidiane Soumah or Tidiane World Music... The appeal I make to Moussa Moise is to tell his officials that a public servant is an employee at our service.” ; “I would say to Moussa Moise that we should stop favouring 2 or 3 artists; that constitutes management outside the State, and in the end it becomes chaos. A department of culture, tourism and handicrafts must work with programmes, and not with individuals.” ; “As I speak to you now, I have decided no longer to address myself to this ministry. As for advances, I find none for the moment.” ; “In a country where there are 33 prefectures, you prefer to favour 1 to 3 artists; that is not a ministry, it is a ghetto... In Guinea we have a governance problem. People confuse political governance and cultural governance. The two must be separated. For 40 years, this is the biggest mistake that keeps coming back, and that is why artists have lost out.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On the Ballets africains and Guinea's branding: “The Ballets africains de Guinée have at all times been the ambassadors of Guinea's African culture... Today in this ministry, you can count on your fingers those who fight for these Ballets africains. All the others, who are supposed to give advice, put their feet in it so that nothing works.” ; “I challenge the Guinean State, I challenge the Ministry of Culture, I challenge every Guinean decision-maker: I know of no artistic instrument of Guinea that can better sell the branding on the planet, apart from the Ballets africains de Guinée.” ; “I do not understand that money is invested in video clips, in bogus concerts by Coronthie in Paris; that is throwing away the Guinean State's money. I think that today Guinean branding is very badly managed abroad.” ; “For me, FODAC, Branding, the Ministry of Culture – that is too much dispersion; a single programme is enough... We had written to the Branding project, to FODAC, to the Ministry of Culture; nobody replied.”

a6352.speaker: Officials of the Ministry of Culture (quoted by Tidiane Soumah)
a6352.name: Officials of the Ministry of Culture (quoted by Tidiane Soumah)
a6352.speech: Are quoted as saying: “you gave the Ballets africains to Tidiane and his associate; they are incapable and we are going to sabotage them.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On the contract and unpaid visa fees: “We signed a 10-year contract, and we had that contract signed under an American label, with a registration number from the American government. All we are asking of Guinea is to pay the production and the visa fees. Since March 2024, the ministry has been incapable of paying the visa fees of the Ballets africains, a group that remained for 17 years without activity. We also had the Ballets africains sign with World Columbia Management International, which is one of the best theatre agencies in the world. No favourable follow-up came of it.” ; “In 37 years, indeed 38 years now, the Ministry of Culture has never financed 1 franc to support Tidiane World Music, while we had spent nearly 13,000,000 US dollars for Guinea... We were only asking for 109,000,000 Guinean francs for insurance fees, visas and other costs, for the 42 members of the Ballets africains, whose list I still hold. These public servants, charged with controlling the funds, are financing billions of Guinean francs for bogus projects.” ; “Whether it wants to or not, a day will come when the Ballets africains will leave Guinea. I am convinced these days that Minister Moussa Moise is doing his best, and only that he is very badly surrounded, by people who do not like us at all.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On how the contract was obtained and his withdrawal: “With the former Secretary General of the ministry François Bourouno... relations were really clean and professional, and that closed my 11 years of struggle... After him, there was total support from Minister Moussa Moise Sylla, from Touré who headed the Guinean agency for shows, and from Sylla who was national director of culture... And quite recently, I felt a wind blowing, which crept in, which sabotaged, and went so far as to cancel the Ballets africains' trip abroad... a plot was being born around Moussa Moise, who no longer had a grip on anything, since his head had been stuffed by a core of officials who revolve around him.” ; “This contract was signed with the AICHA Foundation, which is registered with a number from the American government. It is a signed and notarised contract. Today, they are redoing the whole structure of the Ballets africains, without however consulting the signatory party to the contract. I find all these actions not at all professional, disrespectful... it is for all these reasons, I withdrew. In any case, for 10 years, and on all the stages of the world, the Ballets africains de Guinée belong to the AICHA foundation.” ; “Guinea lost the world stage because of the same conflict, the same officials of the Ministry of Culture... A civil servant, in this case the wife of the late Italo Zambo, went with her husband to see that agency in the United States, which was abnormal, and that led to the cancellation of the Ballets africains' contract and their withdrawal from the world stage.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On his partnership with Mamoudou Condé and the AICHA foundation: “I am a partner with Mamoudou Condé since July 2001, and we still are today. We are partners between ‘World music production’, which is his company in the United States, and ‘Tidiane World Music’... I have the ‘PATISOU’ foundation (Partage Tidiane Soumah)... and he has the ‘AICHA’ foundation, which was born in October 2009, following the sudden death of our daughter, his biological daughter AICHA CONDE... I am the vice-president of this AICHA foundation, Mamoudou Condé is the president, and Sékou Condé is the chairman of the board of directors.” ; “Why did we put the contract in the name of the AICHA foundation? Simply because this foundation has the possibility of asking the American government for aid for training, and for many projects, notably cultural exchange at university level.”

a6352.speaker: Tidiane Soumah, CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.name: Tidiane Soumah
a6352.title: CEO of Tidiane World Music productions and vice-president of the AICHA Foundation
a6352.speech: On the FESTIRAAM project and visas: “Knowing that the foreign partners no longer have confidence in the various ballets and artistic structures at the local level, that is one of the reasons that pushed me to initiate the FESTIRAAM project (International Festival of the Rhythms of Africa and the Antilles of Montreal), to again allow the Ballets africains, the 42 members on the list, each to benefit at most from a 10-year visa, which would encourage them not to flee, or to leave Guinea for good.” ; “I addressed a letter to Canada's immigration minister in order to support the file for the relaunch of the Ballets africains; this approach was well on track, and unfortunately the ill-intentioned blocked everything at the level of the ministry... Faced with that, I have my say, and that is for the good of Guinea and its culture.”

a6378.speaker: Abeba Alemayehu, deputy director of the Public Procurement & Property Disposal Service in charge of procurement and contract administration
a6378.name: Abeba Alemayehu
a6378.title: deputy director of the Public Procurement & Property Disposal Service in charge of procurement and contract administration
a6378.speech: Said dividing the supply into batches was aimed at attracting more companies and getting lower prices. "But after we noticed the price difference for the same quantity," said Abeba, "we decided to award the wheat to a single supplier."

a6378.speaker: Abeba Alemayehu, deputy director of the Public Procurement & Property Disposal Service
a6378.name: Abeba Alemayehu
a6378.title: deputy director of the Public Procurement & Property Disposal Service
a6378.speech: According to her, the current trend of hiring one company for the supply will continue as long as it safeguards the government's interest, accessibility and quality of wheat.

a6378.speaker: Worku Gezahegne, acting director of procurements at the Public Procurement & Property Disposal Service
a6378.name: Worku Gezahegne
a6378.title: acting director of procurements at the Public Procurement & Property Disposal Service
a6378.speech: According to him, the financial opening will be made after 10 days; the technical evaluation is expected to be completed within a week, and the financial evaluation will follow if other bidders do not file a grievance within the mandatory seven-day standstill period.

a6378.speaker: Tesfaye Melaku, lecturer at Bahir Dar University's Department of Economics
a6378.name: Tesfaye Melaku
a6378.title: lecturer at Bahir Dar University's Department of Economics
a6378.speech: Says that the cancellation of the contract could have consequences. "It could lead to bread shortages and inflation," he said, "but this will only happen if the government does not have enough wheat backup."

a6378.speaker: Tesfaye Melaku, lecturer at Bahir Dar University's Department of Economics
a6378.name: Tesfaye Melaku
a6378.title: lecturer at Bahir Dar University's Department of Economics
a6378.speech: Also backs the current procurement procedure, saying that the larger the purchase, the lower the price will be, making it easier to identify an efficient and experienced supplier.

a6378.speaker: Global Agricultural Information Network's 2019 report
a6378.name: Global Agricultural Information Network's 2019 report
a6378.speech: According to it, there are approximately 4.7 million small-scale wheat farmers in Ethiopia, accounting for about 95pc of wheat production, while large-scale commercial farms account for only 5pc of the total production.

a6506.speaker: Villa Somalia (statement)
a6506.name: Villa Somalia (statement)
a6506.speech: According to a statement from Villa Somalia, the leaders reviewed progress on existing agreements and agreed to accelerate joint initiatives in infrastructure, trade, and humanitarian assistance. Both sides emphasized the importance of deepening military and security cooperation to combat terrorism and promote regional stability.

a6506.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Turkish President
a6506.name: Recep Tayyip Erdogan
a6506.title: Turkish President
a6506.speech: Repeated the commitment, stating, “Turkey stands with Somalia in its fight against terrorism. We will continue providing technical, military, and humanitarian assistance to ensure lasting regional stability.”

a6901.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a6901.name: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a6901.speech: Announced that, despite the foreign currency shortage, there have been significant reforms in the financial sector.

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: Said that since he came to NBE there have been many changes ; “About eight months ago our situation was very difficult. The reserve had significantly dropped and the situation regarding settling foreign debts was dire. We were at the edge of defaulting on our external loan settlements” ; “The coming of Abiy has led to new bilateral and multilateral partners who have provided hard currency. This will provide short term relief and enable us to think about further reform plans so that we can solve structural economic problems, hard currency earnings and exports” ; He added that even though there have been delays in payments the government is now settling its loans properly, and providing hard currency to the manufacturing industry, although not as much as needed ; The foreign reserve has also improved, according to the Governor, but he declined to give a specific amount of available forex.

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: Stated the economy was on the brink of a bad fate when the new government came in, but now things have improved, and he expects the country’s economy will register a similar rate as last year ; “If we can provide what the manufacturing industry demands and the agriculture sector is able to meet its targets then economic growth will reach double digits” ; He stated that the government is doing its best to provide foreign currency to the manufacturing sector but it is still less than they need, and amplified that the manufacturing sector also faces other problems like power and skilled labour.

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: “We have worked on several things, and we are undergoing transitions, for instance in the past few months we have worked hard on remittances” ; Said the bank is improving the capacity of staff and establishing groups of experts from local and external professionals for applying several new businesses like bonds and capital markets in the financial sector, and that they are also working on a ten year roadmap.

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: According to the governor the volume of loans in local banks has become quite high: “Due to the instability in the past few years some investors were unable to settle their debt properly so to do so, NBE has been working for extension of the loan settlement period with banks.”

a6901.speaker: Ethiopian investors engaged in similar businesses
a6901.name: Ethiopian investors engaged in similar businesses
a6901.speech: Said the NBE suppliers’ credit scheme created a problem.

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: Said that local investors are supposed to be given priority but the foreign investors believed the country’s law and they have also invested a huge sum so it would be bad if they are not able to make their products because of a hard currency shortage, which can affect the country’s image ; “It is not against the country’s forex law” ; For local investors we are doing our best to help the manufacturing sector get hard currency via a letter of credit (LC), he added.

a6901.speaker: Experts / legal experts
a6901.name: Experts / legal experts
a6901.speech: Experts are arguing that the directive goes against the investment proclamation amended in 2012 ; Legal experts argued that the 769/2012 investment proclamation erroneously mentioned on the central bank directive FXD/47/2017 as ‘679/2012’ on its part one article 2/4 stated that investor means a domestic or a foreign investor that invests in Ethiopia.

a6901.speaker: A business consultant
a6901.name: A business consultant
a6901.speech: “The proclamation indicated that it has not divided local and foreign investors in relation to acquiring external loans,” a business consultant said, “but they claim the central bank directive goes against it.”

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: Said that he is informed about the selling of hard currency by exporters via banks that is illegal ; “The basic problem is the shortage of foreign currency but to tackle illegal activities we are working our hardest and we are also meeting with banks’ presidents to improve the financial sector. If we find someone involved in an illegal act in the foreign market, the actors and the bank will be punished” ; “We have suspicions on illegality in hard currency allocation but have not been able to prove it and we will solve problems if we see any.”

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: “Regarding first come first serve we have not gotten a better option than applying,” he said, regarding the allocation of foreign currency at banks ; “We are working with relevant body that gives licenses to the importers or exporters to solve the problem and identify the real market actors” ; He confirmed that there is a high burden at banks to provide foreign currency.

a6901.speaker: Bankers / bank officials
a6901.name: Bankers / bank officials
a6901.speech: In the past banks wanted the regulatory body to ease the new directive that controlled the way banks handle hard currency; they asked the central bank to give them the responsibility of managing the LC process ; During a meeting between NBE leaders and bank officials in November 2018 bankers expressed their concern about the directive which they claim does not benefit banks or customers; they said illegal actors are still accessing the hard currency and distributing it unfairly.

a6901.speaker: Central bank leaders (NBE)
a6901.name: Central bank leaders (NBE)
a6901.speech: The central bank leaders argued that they applied the directive to create fairness. “NBE has told bankers to come up with a proposal to replace the directive.”

a6901.speaker: Business actors and some bankers
a6901.name: Business actors and some bankers
a6901.speech: Told Capital that individuals who are not seeking hard currency for legitimate reasons, lined up at banks to access foreign currency based on the directive, then they sell their place in line to others.

a6901.speaker: Experts and the private sector / sector actors
a6901.name: Experts and the private sector / sector actors
a6901.speech: Expressed their concern regarding the growing loan interest at banks; the sector actors said that the interest rate has gone up to 25 percent on some types of loans; while the minimum rate which is mainly given to the export business is not small, according to experts in banks. They expressed their concern that it may have lead to inflation and pressure borrowers into debt stress.

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: “Even though it is free for banks and a free market scheme, we shall see if it becomes a problem. But the issue will be answered after a relevant and adequate study” ; “In this regard we have to speak with banks,” he added ; He said that banks, mainly private banks are now providing loans without any challenge.

a6901.speaker: The private sector
a6901.name: The private sector
a6901.speech: Stated that loans particularly from state owned financial firms is lagging.

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: Stated that loan approval from Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) is not as much as is being requested ; “The problem at DBE is very high in relation to debt given for investors mainly for those engaged in rain fed farms” ; He said that agriculture loans amounting to 6.3 billion birr could be repossessed but NBE has ordered DBE to settle the matter legally ; “We did not allow the birr or foreign currency that it wants until it normalizes non-performing loans” ; “Even though they received the loan legally, they took it in an organized manner even calculating how they will not settle the loan.”

a6901.speaker: Yinager Dessie, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Yinager Dessie
a6901.title: governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: Said that in the coming year vast irrigation mainly in low land areas will be applied in the coming years; said the manufacturing sector like textiles and agro processing is growing in the country which will be fed by local input ; “The government has given serious attention to developing the agriculture sector to support the overall economy including solving the hard currency shortage” ; The governor has hinted that irrigation will be a priority for the coming budget year.

a6901.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6901.name: Abiy Ahmed
a6901.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6901.speech: In his meeting with government leaders and prominent international businesspeople, he spoke about the support with irrigation development.

a6966.speaker: Chief Justice's Committee report (Article 146 committee on the petition against Charlotte Osei)
a6966.name: Chief Justice's Committee report (Article 146 committee on the petition against Charlotte Osei)
a6966.speech: Recommended that the Chairperson of the Electoral Commission, Charlotte Osei and her two deputies, Amadu Sulley and Georgina Opoku Amankwaa should be removed from office; according to the report, Charlotte Osei breached procurement laws in the award of several contracts prior to the 2016 elections. "In November 2017, the Honourable Chief Justice of Ghana established a prima facie case on some of the allegations made against the Chairperson of the Electoral Commission as contained in the petition submitted to His Excellency, the President of the Republic." ; "In all, the Chief Justice made facie case against the Chairperson on six of the allegations contained in the said petition."

a6966.speaker: Chief Justice's Committee report (Article 146 committee)
a6966.name: Chief Justice's Committee report (Article 146 committee)
a6966.speech: For all the six allegations, the committee found her culpable and indicated that Charlotte Osei's explanation that she was not aware that she needed to go through procurement for some of the contracts because the monies involved were from donor partners, was untenable. "From the findings we have made on the allegations made against Mrs. Charlotte Osei, the Chairperson of the Electoral Commission, it is clear she breached the Public Procurement Act... In all the procurement activities which we had to investigate, the findings have been that Mrs. Charlotte Osei failed to comply with the Public Procurement Act." ; "The procurement activities include the engagement of Sory@Law and Associates for the Commission, the award of several contracts to STL, the two contracts for the partitioning and consultancy service of the new office block, the three contracts awarded for the construction of pre-fabricated district offices of the Commission and consultancy services thereof; the two contracts awarded to Dreamoval Ltd, and finally the two contracts awarded to Quazar Limited from South Africa. Evidence before the committee showed that all these contracts were awarded by Mrs. Charlotte Osei contrary to the Public Procurement Act."

a6966.speaker: Chief Justice's Committee report (Article 146 committee)
a6966.name: Chief Justice's Committee report (Article 146 committee)
a6966.speech: "On this we disagree with Mrs. Charlotte Osei because we are convinced that procurement forms an important part of the core business of the Electoral Commission. Indeed, without procuring relevant goods and services, the Electoral Commission will find it difficult, if not impossible, to independently conduct free and fair elections in the country. In fact, procurement is so important to the Electoral Commission, that was why no less a person than the Chairperson is made the head of entity of the Commission." ; "if procurement of goods and services was not part of the core business of the Electoral Commission as argued by Mrs. Charlotte Osei, why did she take over the above roles directly when there was a Procurement Unit with a Head in the Electoral Commission? We are of the opinion that Mrs. Charlotte Osei always knew that procurement was a very important part of the core business of the Commission, and that was why she personally took over the above roles." ; "On the whole, Mrs. Charlotte Osei's persistent violation of the Public Procurement showed and in some instance incompetence as found in this report."

a6966.speaker: Chief Justice's Committee report (findings on Allegation No. 5, the USAID-funded Dreamoval contracts)
a6966.name: Chief Justice's Committee report (findings on Allegation No. 5
a6966.title: the USAID-funded Dreamoval contracts)
a6966.speech: Found that before the 2016 general elections the Electoral Commission secured donor support from the USAID through the Ministry of Finance, for US$2,367,500.00 to improve its ICT environment, and that both contracts awarded to Dreamoval were not evaluated by the Tender Evaluation Panel, Entity Tender Committee and Tender Review Panel, nor was approval of the Public Procurement Authority obtained for the restricted tendering method. Held that the Chairperson's claim of ignorance "will not hold simply because the USAID Grant Document cited above, by its paragraph 'E' which is headed 'Procurement' provides as follows; 'The Grantee is responsible for all aspects of the procurements necessary to implement the activity, in accordance with its own procurement procedures'"; concluded that "The non-compliance of the Public Procurement Act for procurement activity funded by donor agencies by the Chairperson can only be explained in terms of her incompetence in understanding the Grant Document she executed with officials of USAID and the Ministry of Finance and provisions of the Public Procurement Act."

a6966.speaker: Chief Justice's Committee report (findings on Allegation No. 6, the Quazar Ltd contracts)
a6966.name: Chief Justice's Committee report (findings on Allegation No. 6
a6966.title: the Quazar Ltd contracts)
a6966.speech: Found that "the allegation that the Chairperson unilaterally awarded contracts to Quazar Ltd is not true," but that the restricted tender method used required prior approval of the Public Procurement Authority under section 38 of Act 663, and that "the fact that the contract was funded by UNDP did not exempt the Commission from complying with the Public Procurement Act"; found the second contract, to develop a logo, was also awarded contrary to the Procurement Act, and that the Chairperson further breached sections 45 and 46 on international competitive tendering since Quazar Ltd was a South African company. "The conduct of the Chairperson in the award of contracts without observing the Public Procurement Act appeared to be a pattern."

a6966.speaker: Chief Justice's Committee report (conclusion)
a6966.name: Chief Justice's Committee report (conclusion)
a6966.speech: Concluded that "the Chairperson, Mrs. Charlotte Osei breached the Public Procurement Act in all the procurement activities for which she was accused. She blatantly breached the Public Procurement Act without any justification"; and that "the conduct of Mrs. Charlotte Osei that violated the Public Procurement Act as demonstrated in this report, constitutes misbehaviour."

a6966.speaker: Charlotte Osei, Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Ghana (testimony)
a6966.name: Charlotte Osei
a6966.title: Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Ghana (testimony)
a6966.speech: Testified that the funds for the two contracts were provided by the USAID and she was unaware that the Commission was to seek the approval of the Public Procurement Authority before awarding the contracts; testified that she personally recommended Dreamoval Ltd, that Dreamoval had to work around the clock to protect the website under cyber-attack, and that she discussed the new bill of US$76,000.00 with USAID, who agreed to pay provided there was a contract for the extra work.

a6966.speaker: Charlotte Osei, Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Ghana (testimony)
a6966.name: Charlotte Osei
a6966.title: Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Ghana (testimony)
a6966.speech: Argued that the core business of the Electoral Commission is not procurement of goods, services or works, so if she is found wanting in the practice of procuring goods and services for the Commission, that per se should not constitute grounds for her removal under Article 146 of the 1992 Constitution.

a6966.speaker: Chief Justice of Ghana (prima facie determination)
a6966.name: Chief Justice of Ghana (prima facie determination)
a6966.speech: "The Public Procurement Act is an enactment which, one may say, is made in pursuance of the principles of probity and accountability expressed in Article 37(1) of the Constitution. It envisages that in the procurement of goods and services with public resources, there must be standard practices which are aimed at fairness and value for money so as to strengthen the national economy. It is for this reason, in my view, that the Act is so detailed and specific in the process and procedures it prescribes." ; "The crucial importance of the standards prescribed by the Act is seen in the fact that, by virtue of section 92 thereof, contravention of the Act is an offence attracting a penalty of a fine not exceeding one thousand penalty units or a term of imprisonment not exceeding five years or to both the fine and imprisonment. Consequently, breach of the requirements of the Act is serious enough, in my view, to amount to [misbehaviour] under Article 146." ; "to my mind, this means that if a person is required by law to perform a certain official function or duty in a particular way but fails or neglect to do so, then the person may be said to have misbehaved in that regard."

a6966.speaker: Halsbury's Laws of England, 4th Edition, Vol. 8, Para 1107 (cited in the Chief Justice's determination)
a6966.name: Halsbury's Laws of England
a6966.title: 4th Edition, Vol. 8, Para 1107 (cited in the Chief Justice's determination)
a6966.speech: "'Behaviour' means in matters concerning the office as to the office itself means exercise of the functions appertaining to the office, or non-attendance, or neglect of or refusal to perform the duties of [the office]."

a6966.speaker: Hamid Kodie Fisa, head of the Donor Desk Unit of the Electoral Commission (testimony)
a6966.name: Hamid Kodie Fisa
a6966.title: head of the Donor Desk Unit of the Electoral Commission (testimony)
a6966.speech: Testified that negotiations for the Dreamoval Ltd contract started in November 2015 and the Chairperson awarded the first contract on 8th February 2016.

a6966.speaker: Hamid Kodie Fisa, head of the Donor Desk Unit of the Electoral Commission (testimony, DW 7)
a6966.name: Hamid Kodie Fisa
a6966.title: head of the Donor Desk Unit of the Electoral Commission (testimony, DW 7)
a6966.speech: Admitted under cross-examination that with [donor] projects the Chairperson was required to follow procurement procedures under the Public Procurement Act.

a7214.speaker: Przemyslaw Bobak, Ambassador and Head of the European Union Mission in Chad
a7214.name: Przemyslaw Bobak
a7214.title: Ambassador and Head of the European Union Mission in Chad
a7214.speech: Hailed “the excellence of the political and diplomatic relations” between Chad and the European Union, recalling the EU’s concrete commitment through humanitarian aid estimated at 134 million euros for the year 2025.

a7214.speaker: Dr Abdoulaye Sabre Fadoul, Minister of State, Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Chadians Abroad
a7214.name: Dr Abdoulaye Sabre Fadoul
a7214.title: Minister of State, Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Chadians Abroad
a7214.speech: In his address, Dr Abdoulaye Sabre Fadoul underlined the uncertain international context, highlighting the constancy of the partnership with the European Union. He praised its attachment “to solidarity between peoples, to multilateralism and to the sovereignty of states, of which territorial integrity is a consequence”.

a7329.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a7329.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.speech: Says the country is prepared to brace the direct and indirect impact of what he terms as "USAID obstacles" ; "Liberia's is resilient and will surely overcome this latest obstacle", Minister Ngafuan told the Voice of America's Day Break Africa program Wednesday, February 19, 2025.

a7329.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a7329.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.speech: Says the lead cancelled project, for local accountability and decentralization, is US$17 million, which was mainly helping the country in domestic resource mobilization: "We have set an ambitious agenda to increase domestic revenue through the Liberia Revenue Authority and USAID was the main partner assisting us to rollout this new tax system from what we call goods and services tax (GST) to Value Added Tax by 2026"; notes the project comes with training, investment assistance and that USAID has been providing support for the government's tax database system or E-tax, which has been assisting in improving government revenue collection in local terrains.

a7329.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a7329.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.speech: Says other projects in education, health and governance, and support to the elections commission which USAID has been supporting through international and local NGOs, are all being affected by the cancellation; acknowledges that there are direct and indirect impacts, noting that other international organizations that had been supported by USAID have scaled down support, with USAID being Liberia's second largest donor next to the World Bank; and recalls USAID support to Liberia from 2021-2029 totaling US$422 million, with an agreement concluded to receive more than US$100 million to support education, health, agriculture and other key areas before everything halted by President Donald Trump.

a7329.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a7329.title: Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
a7329.speech: Asked what Liberia is doing to mitigate the obstacles, says the government has accepted the decision of the United States Government, and discloses that the Ministry of Finance has just concluded and will be submitting to President Boakai and the 55th Legislature short and long-term impacts and what is to be done to address the shocks ; "We will be engaging into some fiscal tightening, mopping up our resources mobilization, among other things. We are going to make sure we reduce losses and abuses, and we will also be engaging our partners in regional organizations; there are conversations in our block on what we are to do to reduce the impact of this cancellation", he assures.

a7329.speaker: Government of Liberia
a7329.name: Government of Liberia
a7329.speech: Says it is prepared to brace direct and indirect impacts of obstacles posed by the departure of USAID.

a7329.speaker: U.S. Ambassador to Liberia (reported by Minister Ngafuan)
a7329.name: U.S. Ambassador to Liberia (reported by Minister Ngafuan)
a7329.speech: Paid Minister Ngafuan a courtesy call and told him that the project for local accountability and decentralization is among several projects that were cancelled under the USAID aid cancellation program.

a7466.speaker: The Catholic Church (official doctrine)
a7466.name: The Catholic Church (official doctrine)
a7466.speech: Asserts that the Roman pontiffs come immediately after Peter, whose position they occupy and whose functions they assume, and that Christ entrusted to Peter supreme authority over the whole Church.

a7466.speaker: Saint Augustine, The Retractations
a7466.name: Saint Augustine
a7466.title: The Retractations
a7466.speech: “I know that subsequently I very often explained the Lord's words: ‘You are Peter and on this rock I will build my Church’ in such a way as to make it understood that the Church is built upon Him whom Peter confessed when he said: ‘You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.’ ... For it was said to him: ‘You are Peter’, and not: ‘You are the rock.’ Now ‘the rock was Christ’.”

a7466.speaker: Encyclopaedia Judaica (Jerusalem, 1971, vol. XV)
a7466.name: Encyclopaedia Judaica (Jerusalem
a7466.title: 1971, vol. XV)
a7466.speech: Speaks of the “great [rabbinical] academies of Babylon” that were operating during the Christian era.

a7466.speaker: John McKenzie, Jesuit, then professor of theology at the University of Notre Dame, The Roman Catholic Church (1969)
a7466.name: John McKenzie
a7466.title: Jesuit, then professor of theology at the University of Notre Dame, The Roman Catholic Church (1969)
a7466.speech: Wrote: “The line of the heads of the Church is not entirely confirmed by historical facts.”

a7466.speaker: New Catholic Encyclopedia (1967), vol. I
a7466.name: New Catholic Encyclopedia (1967)
a7466.title: vol. I
a7466.speech: Admits: “the scarcity of documents explains why we know very little about the original formation of the episcopate.”

a7466.speaker: A Catholic Dictionary (London, 1957, by W. Addis and T. Arnold)
a7466.name: A Catholic Dictionary (London
a7466.title: 1957, by W. Addis and T. Arnold)
a7466.speech: Declares: “The Catholic Church is apostolic because its doctrine is the faith once revealed to the apostles, a faith which it keeps and explains without adding anything to it or taking anything away.”

a7466.speaker: The Catholic Encyclopedia (1912), vol. XV
a7466.name: The Catholic Encyclopedia (1912)
a7466.title: vol. XV
a7466.speech: “The word ‘Trinity’ is the term used to designate the fundamental doctrine of the Christian religion.”

a7466.speaker: The New Encyclopaedia Britannica (1976), Micropaedia, vol. X
a7466.name: The New Encyclopaedia Britannica (1976)
a7466.title: Micropaedia, vol. X
a7466.speech: “The word Trinity does not appear in the New Testament. The doctrine it designates is never explicitly stated there. ... This doctrine took shape gradually, over several centuries and through many controversies.”

a7466.speaker: New Catholic Encyclopedia (1967), vol. XIV
a7466.name: New Catholic Encyclopedia (1967)
a7466.title: vol. XIV
a7466.speech: “Exegetes and biblical theologians, including an increasing number of Catholics, recognize that one should not speak of the Trinity of the New Testament without making serious reservations. At the same time, historians of dogma and systematic theologians admit that when dealing with purely Trinitarian thought one jumps from the origins of Christianity to the last quarter of the fourth century.”

a7466.speaker: Pope Paul VI, encyclical Sacerdotalis Caelibatus (1967)
a7466.name: Pope Paul VI
a7466.title: encyclical Sacerdotalis Caelibatus (1967)
a7466.speech: Reaffirmed the necessity of priestly celibacy, while admitting that “the New Testament, in which the doctrine of Christ and of the Apostles is preserved for us, in no way requires celibacy of sacred ministers... Jesus himself did not make it a precondition for the choice of the Twelve, nor did the Apostles for the men who were placed in charge of the first Christian communities.”

a7466.speaker: Henry Lea, History of Sacerdotal Celibacy in the Christian Church (London, 1932)
a7466.name: Henry Lea
a7466.title: History of Sacerdotal Celibacy in the Christian Church (London, 1932)
a7466.speech: Reports that even before the Christian era Buddhism imposed celibacy on its priests and monks.

a7466.speaker: A. Hislop, The Two Babylons
a7466.name: A. Hislop
a7466.title: The Two Babylons
a7466.speech: Reports that the highest orders of the Babylonian priesthood were devoted to celibacy.

a7466.speaker: Pope Paul VI (1965 address to the United Nations)
a7466.name: Pope Paul VI (1965 address to the United Nations)
a7466.speech: Declared: “The peoples turn to the United Nations as to the only hope for concord and peace: we dare to bring here, together with our own, their tribute of honour and of hope.”

a7466.speaker: E. Watkin, Catholic historian, in Morals and Missiles (London, 1959)
a7466.name: E. Watkin
a7466.title: Catholic historian, in Morals and Missiles (London, 1959)
a7466.speech: Wrote: “Whatever it may cost us, we cannot, in the name of a pseudo-edification or of a dishonest loyalty, deny or pretend to ignore that, in fact, the bishops have always given their support to the wars waged by the government of their country. I know of not a single case in which a national clergy condemned a war by declaring it unjust... Whatever the official theory, in practice Catholic bishops have always taken as their principle in time of war: ‘My country is always right.’”

a7514.speaker: Colonel Daniele Pepe, EUTM MOZ Deputy Mission Force Commander
a7514.name: Colonel Daniele Pepe
a7514.title: EUTM MOZ Deputy Mission Force Commander
a7514.speech: Briefed the Committee on EUTM MOZ' roles, capabilities, mission, current activities and the main ongoing projects within the Headquarters and the three training camps located in Katembe, Chimoio and Mavalane.
